1.meaning: A set of disconnected Arabic letters (the 'broken' or muqaṭṭaʿāt letters) recited individually by name: kāf, hā, yā, ʿayn, ṣād. They open certain chapters and are recited letter by letter rather than read as a word. Their precise import is known only to Allah; scholars note they affirm that the Revelation is composed of the very letters the Arabs themselves used.
1.grammar: These are individual letter-names, not an inflected word; they carry no case ending and are pronounced one by one with elongation. Because they are recited as letters, no grammatical role (subject, object, etc.) attaches to them.

1.meaning: A mention, remembrance, recital, or reminder; the act of bringing something to mind or naming it aloud. The noun spans 'remembrance,' 'commemoration,' and 'a reminder/record' that calls a matter to attention.
1.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or stands as the headword being identified; it often heads a phrase meaning 'a mention/remembrance OF …'.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

2.meaning: Mercy, compassion, loving-kindness; tender care that moves one to relieve and benefit another. As a verbal noun it names the quality and act of showing mercy.
2.grammar: A feminine verbal noun (the tāʾ shows as 't' when joined to what follows). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('mercy OF …') or follows a preposition. Being genitive, it is the possessed/linked term in such a construction.

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: His servant / His slave: a human being owned by and wholly devoted to his Master in worship and obedience. The base word denotes one who serves; the attached pronoun specifies that he belongs to Him (Allah).
4.grammar: A masculine noun with a possessive suffix. The -a ending is the accusative case, marking the word as the direct object of a verb (the one acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case. The suffix -hu means 'his/His,' showing possession by a single male/Divine referent.
4.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, be a devoted slave

5.meaning: Zakariyyā — the proper name of the Prophet Zachariah; a personal name and so without a derived meaning.
5.grammar: A proper name (of a person). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its ending for grammatical case; its role is understood from context.

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: He called out, summoned, or cried aloud to someone — a completed act of calling, often invocation or summons. The Form III pattern adds the sense of directing the call toward another party.
2.grammar: A Form III past-tense verb whose third root letter is weak (a defective verb), so the stem ends in the long vowel written as alif maqṣūra (ـى). It denotes a completed action by 'he' (one male); that 'he' subject is marked by a zero suffix (no added ending), the final long -ā being part of the stem itself, not a separate person/tense marker. Form III characteristically denotes doing an action toward or with another, hence 'to call OUT TO someone.'
2.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w / n-d-y) — to call, summon

3.meaning: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

4.meaning: A call, a calling out, an act of summoning or invoking aloud. As a verbal noun it names the calling itself.
4.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation (indefinite 'a call'). In this case a verbal noun often reinforces its verb ('called WITH a calling') or functions as an object/adverbial; the nunation marks it as indefinite.
4.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w / n-d-y) — to call, summon

5.meaning: Hidden, secret, soft and low; something subtle or concealed from others' notice. Describes a thing done quietly or kept out of view.
5.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation; in this case it typically functions as a describing word agreeing with an accusative noun, or as an adverbial qualifier ('secretly'). The nunation marks it indefinite.
5.root: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden, concealed, faint

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
2.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
3.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

4.meaning: It (he) grew weak, feeble, or frail; strength ebbed away. The verb describes the loss of vigor or firmness in something.
4.grammar: A Form I past-tense verb. The shape marks a completed action with a single masculine subject ('it/he weakened'). The final -a is the standard third-person masculine singular past ending.
4.root: و-ه-ن (w-h-n) — to be weak, feeble, frail

5.meaning: The bone; bone or bones as a structural part of the body, often standing for the frame or strength of the body. The definite article makes it 'the bone(s).'
5.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The prefix al- means 'the.' The final -u is the nominative case, marking the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being described). It can be read as a collective ('bone(s)').
5.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — bone; greatness, magnitude

6.meaning: From me; indicating origin, belonging, or association with the speaker — 'coming from me' or 'of my side'.
6.grammar: The preposition min ('from/of') with the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). An extra n is inserted (giving the doubled 'nn') to join the preposition smoothly to the pronoun. The -ī is the first-person singular pronoun 'me/my'.

7.meaning: And it blazed up / flared / became aflame; the verb pictures something catching fire and spreading, used figuratively of hair turning white as if kindled. The wa- prefix joins it to what precedes.
7.grammar: A Form VIII past-tense verb with the connector wa- ('and'). Form VIII often adds a reflexive/intensive shade ('to catch fire, become inflamed'). The shape marks a completed action by a single masculine subject; the final -a is the third-person masculine singular past ending.
7.root: ش-ع-ل (sh-ʿ-l) — to kindle, ignite, blaze

8.meaning: The head; the topmost part of the body. With the definite article it means 'the head.'
8.grammar: A definite masculine noun; the article (written al-, its 'l' assimilating into the following r) means 'the.' The final -u is the nominative case, marking the word as the subject of a sentence.
8.root: ر-أ-س (r-ʾ-s) — head; top, chief

9.meaning: Grey or white hair; the whiteness of hair that comes with age. The verbal noun names the condition of greying.
9.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation, indefinite. In this case such a noun frequently functions as a specifying complement clarifying respect ('with grey hair' / 'in respect of greying'); the nunation marks it indefinite.
9.root: ش-ي-ب (sh-y-b) — to turn grey, to age

10.meaning: A two-part particle: the connector 'and' joined to 'lam', the negating word that turns a following present-tense verb into a completed past negation — 'and … did not'.

parts.en: did not (negates and puts the verb in the past)

10.grammar: Connector 'wa' ('and') plus the particle 'lam'. 'lam' negates a present-tense verb but shifts its meaning to the past, so 'lam + he finds' means 'he did not find'. It also puts the following verb into the jussive mood (clipping its ending).
10.root: — (particles; no root)

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'I am / I happen to be,' here in a shortened (jussive) form. It is the core verb of being/existing used to link a subject to a state or description. In a shortened form like this it is typically tied to a negation or condition, yielding a sense such as 'I was (not)' or 'should I be.'
11.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular ('I'), in the shortened jussive mood marked by the bare final consonant with a silent stop (sukūn) instead of a vowel. This clipped ending is what a particle of negation or condition produces, so the verb commonly carries a past-negative ('I was not') or conditional ('were I to be') sense rather than a plain present.
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: By/through calling upon You — i.e., through supplication and earnest prayer addressed to You. Combines the preposition 'with/by,' the act of calling/supplicating, and the pronoun 'You.'
12.grammar: A verbal noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by/in'), so it stands in the genitive (-i) as prepositions require. The attached -ka is a possessive pronoun, 'You/Your' (single male addressee), making it 'supplication TO/OF You.'

13.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
13.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

14.meaning: Wretched, miserable, ill-fated, deprived of good; one who fails or is left disappointed. The opposite of blessed and successful.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation, indefinite. In this case it commonly serves as a predicate-complement of certain verbs ('was/became wretched') or describes an accusative noun; the nunation marks it indefinite.
14.root: ش-ق-و / ش-ق-ي (sh-q-w / sh-q-y) — to be wretched, suffer hardship

1.meaning: And indeed I — a connector 'and' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows ('truly, indeed'), with 'I' attached as its subject.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the emphatic particle inna, which lends strong certainty to the statement it opens. The attached -ī ('me/I') is its grammatical subject; inna places the noun or pronoun after it in the accusative.

2.meaning: I feared, was afraid of, or apprehended something. A completed act of fear or wary concern by the speaker.
2.grammar: A Form I past-tense verb (a hollow verb, its middle root weak). The suffix -tu means 'I' did the action in completed (past) time. So it marks a finished act of fearing by the speaker.

3.meaning: Kinsfolk, heirs, guardians, allies, or patrons — relatives and close associates connected by ties of blood, support, or loyalty. The plural denotes such near ones collectively.
3.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural with the article al- ('the'). It is a defective plural whose nominative and genitive end in -ī, while the accusative surfaces as -iya (yāʾ + fatḥa) — the form shown here, marking it as the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative. Its singular is mawlā ('patron, ally, relative').

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: Behind me / after me — what comes following the speaker, whether in place (behind) or in succession (those who come after). Combines 'behind/after' with the pronoun 'me.'
5.grammar: An adverb of place functioning as a noun, with the first-person possessive suffix -ī ('me/my'). The -i before the suffix is the genitive link that such adverbs take when joined to a pronoun, giving 'behind/after me.'
5.root: و-ر-ي / و-ر-أ (w-r-y) — to be behind, to come after

6.meaning: And she was / she became / she came to be; a completed state-of-being verb referring to a single female subject. 'Kāna' and its forms link a subject to a description.
6.grammar: A Form I past-tense 'to be' verb with the connector wa- ('and'). The -at marks a single female subject in completed time ('she was'). The trailing -i is not a case ending but a connecting vowel added so the word flows into what follows. Such verbs put their predicate (the description) into the accusative.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to pass

7.meaning: My wife / my woman; an adult female, here marked as belonging to the speaker. The base noun means 'woman/wife,' and the suffix makes it 'mine.'

parts.en: genitive linking ending before the pronoun

7.grammar: A feminine noun (the tāʾ shows as 't' before the suffix) carrying the first-person possessive -ī ('my'). The -i before it is the linking genitive vowel that appears when a noun is joined to a possessive pronoun, giving 'my wife.'
7.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — relating to a person; (feminine) woman

8.meaning: Barren, infertile; a woman (or thing) that does not bear offspring. The intensive pattern marks it as an inherent characteristic.
8.grammar: An adjective/active-participle form denoting a fixed quality. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation, indefinite. In this case it typically serves as the predicate-complement after a 'to be' verb ('was barren') or describes an accusative noun; the nunation marks it indefinite.
8.root: ع-ق-ر (ʿ-q-r) — to be barren; to wound/hamstring

9.meaning: So grant / so give / bestow! — a command asking that something be given or granted as a gift. The fa- prefix links it to a preceding clause as a result ('so…').
9.grammar: A Form I command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person, with the connector fa- ('so/then') that ties it to what came before as a consequence. Its bare, vowel-less ending is the standard imperative shape — a direct request to 'give/grant.' Often used of bestowing a gift.
9.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, grant, bestow as a gift

10.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
10.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
11.root: — (preposition)

12.meaning: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

parts.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

12.grammar: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
12.root: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

13.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
13.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.

1.meaning: He will inherit me / he will be my heir — to succeed to and carry on what the speaker leaves, whether property or, more deeply, knowledge and prophetic legacy. Combines the verb 'he inherits' with the object 'me.'

parts.en: protective nūn linking to the object

1.grammar: A Form I present/future verb with 'he' as subject (the ya- prefix). The -u is the indicative present ending (an ongoing or future act). The -nī is the object 'me,' joined by a protective nūn that cushions the verb before the 'me' pronoun. So: 'he inherits/will inherit me.'
1.root: و-ر-ث (w-r-th) — to inherit, succeed to, be heir

2.meaning: And he inherits / will inherit; to succeed to and carry on a legacy. The wa- prefix joins it to a preceding verb.
2.grammar: A Form I present/future verb with 'he' as subject (the ya- prefix), joined by wa- ('and'). The final -u is the indicative present ending, signalling an ongoing or future action. Without an attached object pronoun it stands as 'and he inherits/will inherit.'
2.root: و-ر-ث (w-r-th) — to inherit, succeed to, be heir

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: The family, folk, or close people of someone — those belonging to a person's household, following, or kin.
4.grammar: A singular collective noun in the genitive (-i ending), which typically links it to a following noun ('the folk OF …') or follows a preposition. It points to those associated with a named person.
4.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinsfolk (āl is derived from ahl by elision of the hāʾ)

5.meaning: Yaʿqūb (Jacob), the proper name of the Prophet, son of Isḥāq (Isaac) and grandson of Ibrāhīm (Abraham). A personal name, not a word with a meaning derived from a root in Arabic usage.
5.grammar: A proper name treated as 'diptote' (it does not take nunation and uses -a for both the accusative and the genitive). The -a here marks it as a grammatical object or otherwise governed term. As a foreign personal name it carries no Arabic root meaning.

6.meaning: A command meaning 'and make him' or 'and render him' — the imperative of the verb 'to make/place/render,' addressed to a single male, with an attached object pronoun referring to him. Beyond physical 'making,' this verb often means to appoint, designate, or cause something to become a certain way.
6.grammar: A direct command (imperative) addressed to one male. The bare, vowel-less stem 'ij'ʿal' is the command form 'make!'; the helping hamza at the front lets the initial cluster be pronounced. The suffix '-hu' is the object 'him/it.' The opening 'wa' simply links this to what precedes ('and').
6.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

7.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
7.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

8.meaning: Pleasing, well-pleasing, or accepted with approval — one whom another (especially Allah) regards with contentment and favor. It carries the sense of being agreeable and approved, not merely tolerated.
8.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl. The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel plus the 'n' sound of nunation) is the accusative, indefinite case — it commonly marks a word as a direct object, or as a descriptive complement ('as someone pleasing'), and the nunation signals it is indefinite ('a pleasing one').
8.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, contented, satisfied

1.meaning: A direct address: 'O Zakariyyā' — calling out by name to the prophet Zachariah. The 'yā' is the standard particle used to summon or call upon someone.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle of address, equivalent to English 'O…!' The name itself does not change form here. As a proper name of foreign origin it does not take the usual case endings.
1.root: — (proper name)

2.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
2.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

3.meaning: 'We give you good news': to announce glad tidings — something joyful and welcome — to 'you' (one person). The verb conveys delivering happy news that makes the face brighten.
3.grammar: A Form-II verb ('to give glad tidings') in the imperfect, first person plural ('we'), shown by the nu- prefix. The -u before the pronoun is the indicative ending, marking a plain present/future statement. The attached -ka means 'you' (one person), the one receiving the good news.

4.meaning: 'With/of a boy' — a young male child or youth. The base noun denotes a boy or young man, and the attached preposition gives the sense of 'with a boy' or 'of a boy' (as in being given glad tidings of one).
4.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with/of'). Because it follows a preposition, the noun takes the genitive case, shown by the '-in' ending (an 'i' vowel plus the 'n' of nunation). The nunation marks it as indefinite ('a boy').

5.meaning: The noun 'name' joined to the pronoun 'his', meaning 'his name'; the carrying 'u-' is a connecting (helping) vowel sounded only when nothing precedes it.
5.grammar: A masculine noun ('name') with the -u (nominative) ending, the case typical of a subject. The attached '-hu' is a possessive pronoun ('his/its'). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, pronounced only at the start of an utterance.
5.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — name, elevation, that by which a thing is known

6.meaning: Yaḥyā — the personal name of the prophet John (son of Zachariah). As a proper name it functions simply as a label for that individual.
6.grammar: A proper name. Though its form resembles a verb meaning 'he lives,' it functions here purely as a name and is treated as indeclinable — its ending does not shift with grammatical case.
6.root: — (proper name; resonates with ح-ي-ي / ḥ-y-y, to live)

7.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

7.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
7.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: 'We make / we place / we appoint / we provide' — a flexible verb of making, putting in place, rendering something into a state, or assigning.
8.grammar: A present-form verb, first-person plural: 'we make/place.' The final consonant carries no vowel (a sukūn), marking the jussive mood — the clipped form that follows negation ('did not') or conditional/command particles ('let us,' 'so that not'). Its exact force depends on the particle that introduces it.
8.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, set, appoint, render

9.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
9.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
10.root: — (preposition)

11.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
11.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
11.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

12.meaning: A namesake — one who shares the same name as another. By extension the word can also mean someone of equal standing or a peer worthy of the same designation.

parts.en: namesake / one bearing the same name

12.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern. The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — it commonly marks a direct object or a complement, and the nunation shows it is indefinite ('a namesake').

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
2.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
3.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

4.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

5.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
5.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'a boy', 'a young man', or 'a son' — a male child or youth, from infancy up to young manhood.
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun ('a boy'). The final -un ending is nominative with 'tanwīn' (indefinite, 'a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

7.meaning: 'And she was / and it (fem.) was' — the past-tense verb 'to be,' marked for a single female subject, opening with 'and.' This verb sets up a description of a past or ongoing state.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb of 'being.' The '-at' suffix marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('she/it was'). The final '-i' is not a case ending but a connecting vowel added to smooth the join to the next word. The leading 'wa' means 'and.'
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

8.meaning: My wife / my woman; an adult female, here marked as belonging to the speaker. The base noun means 'woman/wife,' and the suffix makes it 'mine.'

parts.en: genitive linking ending before the pronoun

8.grammar: A feminine noun (the tāʾ shows as 't' before the suffix) carrying the first-person possessive -ī ('my'). The -i before it is the linking genitive vowel that appears when a noun is joined to a possessive pronoun, giving 'my wife.'
8.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — relating to a person; (feminine) woman

9.meaning: Barren, infertile; a woman (or thing) that does not bear offspring. The intensive pattern marks it as an inherent characteristic.
9.grammar: An adjective/active-participle form denoting a fixed quality. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation, indefinite. In this case it typically serves as the predicate-complement after a 'to be' verb ('was barren') or describes an accusative noun; the nunation marks it indefinite.
9.root: ع-ق-ر (ʿ-q-r) — to be barren; to wound/hamstring

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and indeed / and already' — wa- ('and') joined to qad, a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that something has certainly and already happened.
10.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to the particle qad. With a past-tense verb, qad emphasizes that the action has truly and already taken place ('has indeed …'); with a present-tense verb it can instead mean 'sometimes / may'. It is a fixed particle with no case ending.
10.root: — (particle)

11.meaning: 'I have reached' or 'I have attained' — the past-tense verb 'to reach/arrive at,' marked for an 'I' subject. It is used both physically (reaching a place) and figuratively (reaching an age, limit, or condition).
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-tu' marks the first-person singular subject — 'I' did the action. The verb stem itself carries the completed/past sense.
11.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, arrive at, attain

12.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

13.meaning: Old age — the advanced stage of life, with its weakness and the passing of one's prime; also greatness or seniority in years. Here it carries the sense of being well advanced in age.
13.grammar: A definite singular noun. The -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
13.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large; to grow old, advance in years

14.meaning: Extreme old age — having grown very old, to the point of frailty and decline. The word denotes advanced, decrepit age and the physical weakness that comes with it.
14.grammar: A verbal noun. The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — here it typically functions as a specifying complement (telling 'in respect of what,' e.g. reaching old age), and the nunation marks it as indefinite.
14.root: ع-ت-و (ʿ-t-w) — to exceed bounds; to be intractable/obstinate; to become very old

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
2.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
2.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

3.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
3.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
4.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

5.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'upon / on / over' fused with the attached pronoun 'me,' giving 'upon me / against me / on my account.' The base preposition signals being on top of, responsible for, or burdened by something, and can also carry the sense of something owed by or weighing against a person.
6.grammar: A preposition with the first-person singular pronoun 'me' attached. When the pronoun 'me' joins this preposition, its form shifts so the two merge into 'ʿalayya.' Pronouns attached to prepositions always take the object form ('me,' not 'I'), and no case ending applies to them.

7.meaning: Easy, light, or simple — something that poses no difficulty. The word describes a matter that is effortless or trifling for the one undertaking it.
7.grammar: An adjective on the fayʿil pattern. The '-un' ending (a 'u' vowel with nunation 'n') is the nominative, indefinite case — it commonly marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('it is easy'), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
7.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — to be easy, light, of little difficulty

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and indeed / and already' — wa- ('and') joined to qad, a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that something has certainly and already happened.
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to the particle qad. With a past-tense verb, qad emphasizes that the action has truly and already taken place ('has indeed …'); with a present-tense verb it can instead mean 'sometimes / may'. It is a fixed particle with no case ending.
8.root: — (particle)

9.meaning: 'I created you' — the past-tense verb 'to create' with an 'I' subject and a 'you' (single male) object. The root denotes bringing into being and shaping, fashioning something from nothing.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-tu' marks the first-person singular subject ('I'), and the further suffix '-ka' is the object 'you' (addressing one male). The stem carries the completed/past sense.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
10.root: — (preposition)

11.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
11.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
11.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

12.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
12.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

13.meaning: It/she is or comes to be — a verb of being expressing existence or a state, in a shortened form of the verb 'to be.'
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of being in the shortened (jussive) mood. The 'ta-' prefix marks a third-person feminine singular (or 'it') subject. The jussive drops the final vowel — and here even the final 'n' of 'takun' falls away — giving the clipped sense 'is/was (not),' a form occurring after particles of negation or condition.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

14.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
14.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
2.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: Make! / Set up! / Appoint! A command to bring something into being, fashion it, or designate something as something else.

parts.en: helping vowel for the command (hamzat al-waṣl)
make / appoint (command stem, all three root letters)

3.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'make!' The opening i- is a helping vowel (hamzat al-waṣl) that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced; it is not part of the root. The stem جۡعَلۡ carries all three root letters (j-ʿ-l), and its final consonant takes a silent ending (sukūn), the normal way an imperative is closed off.

4.meaning: For me / to me / mine — a preposition meaning 'to/for' fused with the first-person 'me', expressing possession, benefit, or attribution toward the speaker.
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). Together they express that something belongs to, is owed to, or is for the benefit of the speaker.

5.meaning: 'A sign' — a token, mark, or proof that points to something beyond itself; a miraculous indication, a lesson, or an evidence. (The same word also denotes a verse of the Qur'an.)
5.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with 'tanwīn', the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or as the thing one is being made or named, and signals 'a / an' rather than 'the'.
5.root: ا-ي-ي / ء-ي-ي (’-y-y) — sign, mark, token

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

7.meaning: Your sign — a 'sign' meaning a token, mark, miracle, or evidence pointing to a greater truth (the same word used for a verse of the Qur'an), here possessed by a single male addressee.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun carrying the nominative -u ending (typical of a sentence's subject) with the possessive suffix -ka ('your', addressing one male). The feminine ending appears as 't' (āyat-) before the pronoun.
7.root: ا-ي-ي / ء-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

8.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
8.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

9.meaning: That you speak / converse — the verb for speaking to or talking with someone, in an intensive form implying real, mutual conversation, addressed to a single male.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb, second person masculine singular ('you speak'), built on the intensive form-II pattern (kallama). The prefix tu- marks 'you (m. sg.)'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after particles like 'that/so that' and gives the sense of an intended or hypothetical act rather than a plain statement.

10.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
10.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

11.meaning: "three" — the cardinal number 3.
11.grammar: A cardinal number. The ending -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case; numbers in this construct state precede the thing counted and link to it ("three of …"), with the counted noun following in the genitive. The -a is the case ending shown in the transliteration.
11.root: ث-ل-ث (th-l-th) — three

12.meaning: Nights — the plural of 'night,' the dark period between sunset and dawn. It can also denote a span of days counted by their nights.
12.grammar: A plural noun that is normally a diptote (it takes a reduced set of endings) and ends in a weak letter (yā'). Under the rule for such weak-final words in the indefinite, the final yā' drops and '-in' is added: here the '-in' is the genitive, indefinite ending, with the nunation marking it as indefinite ('nights').

13.meaning: Even, straight, and well-balanced — sound and upright in form, level and properly proportioned, walking erect on a straight course.
13.grammar: An adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern meaning 'even / straight / sound'. The final '-an' (tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative, a form often used to describe the state or manner of someone or something ('walking upright, on a level path').
13.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, level, straight, well-proportioned

1.meaning: 'Then he came out / went forth' — the past-tense verb 'to go out, emerge, depart,' marked for a single male subject, opening with 'then/so' to mark sequence.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with a third-person singular masculine subject built in ('he'). The final '-a' is the standard past-tense vowel for this form, not a case marker. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then/so' and signals that this follows on from what came before.
1.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, emerge

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

3.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
3.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: A prayer niche, sanctuary, or private chamber — an inner place set apart for worship, devotion, or retreat; the front recess of a place of prayer.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the prayer chamber'), marked by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -i vowel is genitive, which typically follows a preposition (e.g. 'in / from the chamber') or links the word to a preceding noun.
5.root: ح-ر-ب (ḥ-r-b) — war, fighting, combat; the noun miḥrāb derives from it as a 'place of struggle / combat'

6.meaning: 'Then he revealed / signaled / inspired' — the past-tense verb of conveying something swiftly and discreetly, marked for a single male subject, with 'then/so' at the front. The root spans divine revelation as well as a subtle sign, gesture, or hint between people.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb of the form-IV (causative) pattern, with a built-in third-person singular masculine subject ('he'). The verb ends in a weak letter written as a long 'ā.' The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then/so,' marking sequence.
6.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, inspire, signal subtly

7.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
7.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
8.root: — (particle; no root)

9.meaning: A command 'glorify!' / 'declare (Allah's) perfection!' addressed to a group — to proclaim that Allah is far above any flaw or imperfection. It combines praise with declaring transcendence.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) on the intensive form-II pattern, addressed to a group of males. The '-ū' ending marks a plural 'you all' as the ones commanded. (The written final alif after the wāw is silent.)
9.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glorify, declare (Allah) free of all imperfection

10.meaning: Morning, daybreak, the early part of the day — the time from dawn until mid-morning.

parts.en: accusative ending on feminine noun (with nunation)

10.grammar: A feminine noun (its feminine ending is the tied-tā', pronounced '-t-' before the case vowel). The '-an' accusative ending here typically marks a time expression ('in the morning'), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
10.root: ب-ك-ر (b-k-r) — early morning, to be early

11.meaning: Evening, late afternoon, the close of the day — the period from after noon until nightfall. Here it appears with 'and' joining it to a preceding word.
11.grammar: A noun with the '-an' accusative, indefinite ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n'). This ending commonly marks a time expression ('in the evening'). The opening 'wa' means 'and.'
11.root: ع-ش-و / ع-ش-ي (ʿ-sh-w/y) — evening, the latter part of the day

1.meaning: A direct address: 'O Yaḥyā' — calling out by name to the prophet John. 'Yā' is the particle used to call or summon someone.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction: 'yā' is the particle of address ('O…!') and 'Yaḥyā' is the name being called. As a proper name it is indeclinable — its ending does not change with case.
1.root: — (proper name; resonates with ح-ي-ي / ḥ-y-y, to live)

2.meaning: 'Take! / Hold! / Adopt!' A direct command to one person to take hold of, seize, accept, or adopt something.
2.grammar: A singular imperative ('you, take'). The base command is khudh; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster, not a case ending. The verb comes from a root whose initial hamza is dropped in the command form.
2.root: ء-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp, adopt

3.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

4.meaning: "With strength / firmness / resolve" — quwwa is power, strength, or might; with the prefix it means 'with strength', i.e. firmly and resolutely.
4.grammar: The preposition 'bi' ('with, by means of') attached to a feminine noun. The -in ending (tanwīn) marks the noun as indefinite ('a strength') and in the genitive case — the form always required after a preposition.

5.meaning: 'And We gave/granted him' — a verb of bestowing or handing over something, with 'We' as the giver and 'him' as the recipient. The root conveys the act of bringing or delivering a thing to someone so that they come to possess it.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to give/bring to'). The suffix -nā is the subject 'we' (the doers of the giving). The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it' (the one given to). So the form packs subject and object into one word: 'we-gave-him'.
5.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this causative form, to bring/give

6.meaning: Sound judgment, wisdom, and the authority to decide rightly — discernment in distinguishing truth from falsehood and ruling or acting accordingly. The word spans judgment, governance, and wisdom.
6.grammar: A definite noun (the prefix 'al-' = 'the'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb. Because the word is made definite by 'al-', there is no nunation.
6.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide wisely, govern

7.meaning: A child, young boy, or infant — a male in early childhood. The word denotes someone of tender, pre-adult age.
7.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern. The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — it often marks a circumstantial state ('while [still] a child') or a direct object, and the nunation shows indefiniteness.
7.root: ص-ب-و / ص-ب-ي (ṣ-b-w/y) — childhood, to be young/inclined

1.meaning: Tenderness, compassion, heartfelt affection and mercy — a deep, gentle warmth toward another. It denotes loving kindness that wells up from the heart.
1.grammar: A noun with the '-an' accusative, indefinite ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n'). This ending commonly marks a direct object or a bestowed thing. The leading 'wa' means 'and.'
1.root: ح-ن-ن (ḥ-n-n) — to feel tenderness, compassion, yearning

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

3.meaning: 'From Us', 'from Our presence', 'from Ourselves' — denotes something proceeding directly from a giver's own self or side. 'Ladun' means 'the presence/side of', and the ending here ties it to 'Us'.
3.grammar: An invariable noun of place/source ('ladun', 'the presence of') with the attached 'us'; the doubled-n reflects 'ladun' meeting the 'nā' ('us'). It conveys 'from Our own side', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

4.meaning: Purity and inner cleansing — growth in goodness and freedom from corruption. The same word also names the obligatory charity (zakāh), which both purifies wealth and the soul; its core sense is purification and wholesome growth.

parts.en: accusative ending on feminine noun (with nunation)

4.grammar: A feminine noun (the feminine tied-tā' is pronounced '-t-' before the ending). The '-an' accusative, indefinite ending commonly marks a direct object or a granted thing, and the nunation shows it is indefinite. The opening 'wa' means 'and.'
4.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure, to grow wholesomely

5.meaning: And it was / came to be — a linking verb expressing past existence or state ('was', 'used to be'); often introduces a description that held true.
5.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus kāna, a past-tense linking verb built on a hollow root (middle letter a weak wāw). The final -a marks a single masculine subject 'he/it'. As a 'to be' verb it connects a subject with a description of its past state — 'and he/it was …'.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to be

6.meaning: God-conscious, devout, and guarding against wrong — one filled with taqwā: a reverent awareness of Allah that makes a person shield himself from sin and do what is right. It is far richer than mere 'righteous'; it is mindful, protective piety.
6.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — it commonly marks a descriptive complement ('as one who is God-conscious') or a predicate, and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
6.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (oneself from harm/wrong)

1.meaning: Dutiful, kind, and devoted — especially toward one's parents. The word describes someone abundant in goodness, devotion, and benevolent treatment of others; it can also mean truly righteous and pious.
1.grammar: An adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) on the pattern faʿl, with the final root letter doubled (ب-ر-ر → بَرّ). The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — it commonly marks a descriptive complement or predicate, and the nunation shows it is indefinite. The leading 'wa' means 'and.'
1.root: ب-ر-ر (b-r-r) — to be dutiful, devoted, abundantly good

2.meaning: A combination meaning roughly 'with/toward his two parents (father and mother together)'. The dual noun wālidān refers specifically to the two who gave one birth — one's father and mother as a pair — and the attached pronoun makes them 'his'.
2.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('with, to, toward'). The stem is a dual noun (referring to exactly two — a father and mother together); its dual ending appears as -ay rather than -ān because it stands in the genitive/accusative form, which is also what the preposition bi- requires. The final -hi is the attached possessive pronoun 'his' (the -i vowel is the form this pronoun takes after an -i sound).
2.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

3.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
3.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

4.meaning: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be / to exist / to happen', in a shortened (jussive) shape often carrying the sense 'it is' or, with a negating particle, 'it is not / was not'.
4.grammar: The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The verb is in the jussive mood, shown by the bare final consonant with sukūn (-n, no vowel) and the dropped long vowel of the root; this clipped form appears after certain particles (such as those that negate or command) and signals it is governed by one of them rather than standing as a plain statement.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

5.meaning: A tyrant; an overbearing, domineering person who forces his will on others, haughty and merciless. The pattern is intensive, conveying someone whose oppressive power is a defining trait. When used of Allah, the same root word means the All-Compeller, but in human reference it is blameworthy arrogance.
5.grammar: This is a noun on the intensive pattern faʿʿāl, which marks an ingrained or habitual quality ('one who constantly compels/oppresses'). The final -an (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending: it marks the word as 'a tyrant' (indefinite) and signals it is functioning as an object or predicate rather than a subject.
5.root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r) — to compel, force, restore by force; might, dominance

6.meaning: Disobedient, rebellious; one who refuses to comply and persistently defies. The intensive form points to defiance as a settled disposition rather than a single act.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a strong or characteristic quality ('thoroughly disobedient'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking it as an indefinite word in object/predicate position.

1.meaning: 'And peace' — salām denotes peace, safety, soundness, and freedom from harm and defect; it is also the greeting of wellbeing and security. The wa- attaches it to what precedes.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connector 'and'. The stem salām is a noun for peace and security. The final -un (tanwīn) is the indefinite nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as a standalone subject of a statement ('peace [be]…').
1.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — to be safe, sound, whole; peace, submission

2.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
2.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

3.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
3.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

4.meaning: 'He was born' — a passive past-tense verb describing the event of being brought into the world / given birth to.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice: the internal vowel pattern u–i (wulida rather than active walada) shows the action was done to the subject — 'he was born' rather than 'he gave birth'. The final -a with no suffix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he').
4.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

5.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

6.meaning: 'He dies' / 'he will die' — a present-tense verb denoting the act of dying, the departure of life.
6.grammar: A present/future-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood for a plain statement of fact ('he dies / will die'), as opposed to endings that would signal command or dependence on another particle.

7.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

8.meaning: 'He is raised / will be raised (up)' — a passive present-tense verb. The root carries the sense of being sent forth or stirred into action, and in the religious sense of being resurrected and brought back to life.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense (imperfect) verb in the passive voice. The prefix yu- (with the u-vowel and the internal pattern) marks both third-person masculine singular ('he') and the passive ('is/will be raised' — the action is done to him). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement.
8.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send, raise up, rouse; resurrect

9.meaning: Alive, living; possessing life. The form can also carry the fuller sense of being vigorously, truly alive.
9.grammar: An adjective on the faʿl pattern, here showing as ḥayy through contraction of the final weak letters (ḥayiy → ḥayy). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending; in this kind of word it commonly marks a descriptive state of someone — i.e. that they are/do something 'while alive' or 'as a living one'.

1.meaning: 'And mention / and remember / and recall' — a command to bring something to mind and call it out, whether by remembering it inwardly or speaking of it aloud.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- is 'and'. The stem is a command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'mention / remember!'. The helping vowel at the start (the alif pronounced u-) is needed to begin the word, and the final consonant carries a vowelless ending (sukūn), which is the typical close of a singular command.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind; remembrance

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
3.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

4.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
4.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

5.meaning: 'When / at the time when' — a particle pointing to a moment or circumstance in time, introducing the situation in which something happens. Here it carries its connecting vowel.
5.grammar: A time particle ('when'). It is indeclinable — its core form is 'idh', and the final -i here is simply a helping vowel added so the word joins smoothly to what follows (avoiding two unvowelled consonants meeting). It introduces a clause describing the time or circumstance of an event.

6.meaning: 'She withdrew / she secluded herself / she retreated' — a past-tense verb for drawing apart from others to a distant or private place. The form adds a sense of doing this to or for oneself.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in a reflexive/self-directed pattern (Form VIII, iftaʿala), where the inserted -t- gives the sense of doing the action for or upon oneself ('she took herself away'). The opening alif is a helping vowel needed to start the word. The suffix -at (here -t before the vowelless ending) marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she').
6.root: ن-ب-ذ (n-b-dh) — to cast off, throw aside; withdraw, set apart

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: Her people / her household — those belonging to her: her family, kin, or the folk to whom she pertains.
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'the people belonging to' someone, here in a possessive construction. The -i ending is genitive, the case used when a word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive ('… of …'). The attached -hā is the pronoun 'her' (or 'its,' feminine).
8.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinfolk, the people proper to a place or thing

9.meaning: A place, location, or spot; the position where something is situated.
9.grammar: A noun of place built on the m- pattern (nouns beginning with ma- often denote the place of an action). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, here typically marking 'a place' as the destination or object of a verb of going/taking.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to be

10.meaning: Eastern; belonging to or lying toward the east, the direction of sunrise.
10.grammar: An adjective of relation (nisba): the -iyy ending turns the noun 'east' into 'eastern / pertaining to the east'. The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, agreeing with an indefinite noun it describes when that noun is in object position.
10.root: ش-ر-ق (sh-r-q) — to rise (of the sun); the east, sunrise

1.meaning: 'So/then she took / adopted / set up (for herself)' — a past-tense verb for taking something and making it one's own. The pattern gives a self-directed sense, and the prefix fa- links it as a consequence ('and so…').
1.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so / then', marking what follows as a result or next step. The stem is a past-tense (perfect) verb on the reflexive Form VIII pattern (ittaʿala), giving the sense of taking something for oneself; its doubled letter and opening helping-vowel alif belong to this form. The suffix -at (here -t) marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she').
1.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, adopt

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: 'Apart from them / besides them / below them'. The base word 'dūn' marks something other than or short of a reference point; with 'them' attached it means 'other than those people' or 'lower/nearer than them'.

parts.en: genitive ending (after this word, before the pronoun)

3.grammar: An adverb/preposition of relation ('apart from, besides, short of') with the attached pronoun -him ('them', masculine plural). The -i vowel is the genitive linking the word to the pronoun; the form -him (with i-vowel) is the regular shape the pronoun takes after a genitive/'i' sound.

4.meaning: A barrier, screen, or veil — something that partitions, conceals, or blocks off, standing between two things.
4.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb — the thing acted upon (e.g. something placed or set). The noun names a partition that screens off or conceals.
4.root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b) — to veil, screen, block, conceal from view

5.meaning: 'So/then We sent' — a past-tense verb of sending or dispatching, with the prefix fa- marking it as a consequence and the ending marking 'we' as the doer.
5.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so / then'. The stem is a past-tense (perfect) verb on the causative Form IV pattern (afʿala — 'to make something go', i.e. to send). The suffix -nā is the attached subject pronoun 'we', marking a first-person plural doer ('we sent').
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; messenger, message

6.meaning: Toward it / to her — the directional preposition 'ilā' ('to, toward'), expressing motion or inclination toward a goal, here joined to a feminine 'it/her'.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/toward', whose form shifts from 'ilā' to 'ilay-' when a pronoun attaches. The suffix -hā is the feminine singular object ('it/her'). It marks the endpoint or direction of motion or leaning.

7.meaning: 'Our spirit' — rūḥ is the spirit, the breath of life, the immaterial principle by which living things live; it is also used for a noble angelic being. The attached pronoun makes it 'our'.
7.grammar: The stem rūḥ ('spirit') carries the short vowel -a before the suffix, the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The final -nā is the attached possessive pronoun 'our'.
7.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — spirit, breath, wind; rest, refreshment

8.meaning: 'So/then he took on the likeness / appeared in the form (of)' — a past-tense verb meaning to represent oneself as, or assume the shape and likeness of, something. The prefix fa- links it as 'and so…'.

parts.en: he took on the likeness / appeared in form

8.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so / then'. The stem is a past-tense (perfect) verb on the reflexive Form V pattern (tafaʿʿala), where the ta- prefix and doubled middle letter give the sense of making oneself into a likeness ('he formed himself into / presented himself as'). The final -a with no suffix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he').
8.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble, be like; likeness, example

9.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
9.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

10.meaning: 'A human being / a mortal man' — a member of humankind, emphasising ordinary flesh-and-blood humanity as opposed to something angelic or divine.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case (the object or the thing being described/named) and the absence of 'the' ('a human being'). 'bashar' denotes humankind with stress on bodily, mortal nature.
10.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — human skin; humankind, mortal nature

11.meaning: Even, straight, and well-balanced — sound and upright in form, level and properly proportioned, walking erect on a straight course.
11.grammar: An adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern meaning 'even / straight / sound'. The final '-an' (tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative, a form often used to describe the state or manner of someone or something ('walking upright, on a level path').
11.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, level, straight, well-proportioned

1.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: 'I seek refuge / protection' — to take shelter in and appeal to someone (Allah) for safety against an evil or danger. Conveys turning to a protector for guarding.

parts.en: seek refuge / take shelter (stem, ending in the indicative vowel -u)

3.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to seek refuge'. The opening alif (a-) marks the subject as 'I'. The stem ends in the third root letter ذ, which carries the final short vowel -u; this -u is the indicative ending, signalling a real, ongoing action — a plain statement ('I seek refuge') rather than a command or a 'that…' form.
3.root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh) — to seek refuge, take shelter, protect oneself

4.meaning: By the All-Merciful — al-Raḥmān, a name of Allah denoting boundless, all-embracing mercy that overflows to the whole of creation; a quality so intense it functions almost as a proper name.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, in') joined to the definite name al-Raḥmān. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition. The name follows an intensive pattern signifying mercy that is vast, overflowing, and all-encompassing.

5.meaning: 'Than you' / 'from you' — the preposition meaning 'from, of, than' attached to the pronoun 'you' (one male).
5.grammar: Preposition + attached pronoun. Min means 'from/of' and is the standard word used after a comparative to mean 'than.' The suffix -ka is the second-person singular masculine pronoun 'you' (the -a vowel marks it as masculine; a female addressee would be -ki).
5.root: — (a particle/preposition; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
6.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

7.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

8.meaning: God-conscious, devout, and guarding against wrong — one filled with taqwā: a reverent awareness of Allah that makes a person shield himself from sin and do what is right. It is far richer than mere 'righteous'; it is mindful, protective piety.
