8.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — it commonly marks a descriptive complement ('as one who is God-conscious') or a predicate, and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
8.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (oneself from harm/wrong)

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
3.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

4.meaning: A messenger or envoy: one who is sent by another to deliver a message or carry out a commission. In Qur'anic usage it most often denotes a prophet sent by Allah with revelation.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word identified by a linking verb ('… is …').

5.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a female). Rabb means the Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings a thing to its completion; it combines ownership, care, and authority in one term. The attached pronoun makes it 'your', addressed to a single female.
5.grammar: The stem rabb carries the -i (genitive) ending, which typically appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun ('… of your Lord'). The final -ki is the attached possessive pronoun 'your', specifically addressing a single female (the -i vowel marks it feminine, as opposed to -ka for a male).
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

6.meaning: 'So that I may give / bestow / grant' — the verb means to give freely as a gift, with no expectation of return; the prefix li- expresses purpose ('in order that').
6.grammar: The prefix li- means 'so that / in order to', expressing purpose. The a- prefix on the verb marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). Because li- is a particle of purpose, it puts the present-tense verb into the subjunctive, shown by the final -a ending (instead of the plain -u); this -a signals that the action is the intended goal ('that I may give') rather than a standalone fact.
6.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, grant, bestow a gift

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'for you' or 'to you' (addressed to a single female) — the preposition li- ('for/to') joined to the pronoun for 'you'.
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to'), joined to the attached pronoun -ki ('you'). The lam regularly takes the vowel -a (fatḥa) before any attached pronoun other than the first-person 'me', so la- + -ki is the standard paradigm form. The -ki ending specifically marks a single female addressee, so the whole means 'for you (a woman)'.
7.root: — (particle with pronoun)

8.meaning: 'A boy / a youth / a young lad' — a male child or young servant who has not yet reached full manhood. Indefinite: 'a boy.'
8.grammar: An indefinite noun ending in -an (accusative 'tanwīn'). The -an marks the accusative state — typically the object of a verb — and the final 'n' sound signals indefiniteness ('a boy,' not 'the boy').
8.root: غ-ل-م (gh-l-m) — youth, a young male

9.meaning: Pure, innocent, righteous; cleansed of fault and morally sound, also carrying the sense of one who grows in goodness and blessing.
9.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a firm or characteristic quality ('thoroughly pure'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking an indefinite word in object or descriptive position.
9.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure, to grow, to increase in goodness; purity

1.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

2.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
2.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

3.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

4.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
4.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'a boy', 'a young man', or 'a son' — a male child or youth, from infancy up to young manhood.
5.grammar: A masculine singular noun ('a boy'). The final -un ending is nominative with 'tanwīn' (indefinite, 'a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
5.root: غ-ل-م (gh-l-m) — youth, a young male

6.meaning: A two-part particle: the connector 'and' joined to 'lam', the negating word that turns a following present-tense verb into a completed past negation — 'and … did not'.

parts.en: did not (negates and puts the verb in the past)

6.grammar: Connector 'wa' ('and') plus the particle 'lam'. 'lam' negates a present-tense verb but shifts its meaning to the past, so 'lam + he finds' means 'he did not find'. It also puts the following verb into the jussive mood (clipping its ending).

7.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he touches me / he has contact with me'. It denotes physical touching or contact directed at the speaker.
7.grammar: A present/future verb (Form I, massa, 'to touch'), showing its unmerged base mas-as. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ending appears in jussive/short form (sukūn on the last root letter) — the form used after particles of negation ('has not touched') or condition ('if … touch'). The suffix -nī ('me') includes the protective nūn that attaches object pronouns to verbs.
7.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact

8.meaning: 'A human being, a mortal man' — bashar denotes humankind as flesh-and-blood mortals. It emphasizes the human, bodily nature of a person.
8.grammar: A noun (also usable collectively for 'mankind'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a human being'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence (e.g. the one who acts) or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied.
8.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — skin/outer surface; humankind, mortal

9.meaning: A two-part particle: the connector 'and' joined to 'lam', the negating word that turns a following present-tense verb into a completed past negation — 'and … did not'.

parts.en: did not (negates and puts the verb in the past)

9.grammar: Connector 'wa' ('and') plus the particle 'lam'. 'lam' negates a present-tense verb but shifts its meaning to the past, so 'lam + he finds' means 'he did not find'. It also puts the following verb into the jussive mood (clipping its ending).

10.meaning: 'I am / I be' — a shortened present-tense form of the verb 'to be', stating that the speaker is (or, with a negator, is not) in some state.
10.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) form of the verb 'to be' (kāna). The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). This is a shortened (jussive/apocopated) form: the expected final -n has been dropped and the verb ends bare, which happens after a negative or conditional particle — so it characteristically means 'I am not / let me not be' in such a setting rather than a plain 'I am'.
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, become

11.meaning: An unchaste woman; one who transgresses sexual bounds. The root sense is overstepping limits and rebellion, applied here to immoral, licentious conduct.
11.grammar: A noun/adjective on the faʿīl pattern conveying an ingrained quality. The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking it as indefinite and in object or predicate position ('[I have not been] an unchaste woman').
11.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to exceed bounds, transgress, act wrongfully; sexual immorality

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: 'Thus, in this way, like that' — a demonstrative expression of manner addressed to a female, meaning 'so it is' or 'in such a manner', pointing to the way something happens.
2.grammar: A compound of the comparison particle ka- ('like, as') with the demonstrative dhālika ('that'), forming an adverb of manner ('thus, like that'). The final -ki marks the addressee as a single female (the -ka form addresses a male). This element of address does not change for case; it is fixed.

3.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
3.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a female). Rabb is the Lord, Master, and Sustainer — owner, nurturer, governor, and the one who brings each thing to completion. The attached pronoun makes it 'your', addressed to a single female.
4.grammar: The stem rabb carries the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks the word as the subject — the one performing the action or being spoken about ('your Lord [says/does]…'). The final -ki is the attached possessive pronoun 'your', addressing a single female (contrast -ka for a male).
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

5.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'upon / on / over' fused with the attached pronoun 'me,' giving 'upon me / against me / on my account.' The base preposition signals being on top of, responsible for, or burdened by something, and can also carry the sense of something owed by or weighing against a person.
6.grammar: A preposition with the first-person singular pronoun 'me' attached. When the pronoun 'me' joins this preposition, its form shifts so the two merge into 'ʿalayya.' Pronouns attached to prepositions always take the object form ('me,' not 'I'), and no case ending applies to them.

7.meaning: Easy, light, or simple — something that poses no difficulty. The word describes a matter that is effortless or trifling for the one undertaking it.
7.grammar: An adjective on the fayʿil pattern. The '-un' ending (a 'u' vowel with nunation 'n') is the nominative, indefinite case — it commonly marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('it is easy'), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
7.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — to be easy, light, of little difficulty

8.meaning: 'And so that We may make / appoint / render him' — combines 'and', a purpose marker 'so that', the verb 'to make/appoint/turn (something) into', the 'we' subject, and 'him' as the object.
8.grammar: The prefix wa- is 'and'; li- expresses purpose ('so that'). The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). Because li- is a purpose particle, the present-tense verb is in the subjunctive, shown by the -a ending on the verb (jaʿala-), signaling an intended goal ('that we may make') rather than a plain fact. The final -hu is the attached object pronoun 'him'.
8.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

9.meaning: 'A sign' — a token, mark, or proof that points to something beyond itself; a miraculous indication, a lesson, or an evidence. (The same word also denotes a verse of the Qur'an.)
9.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with 'tanwīn', the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or as the thing one is being made or named, and signals 'a / an' rather than 'the'.

10.meaning: For the people, for mankind, for humankind. The preposition 'for/to' joined to 'the people' as a collective term for human beings.
10.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') prefixed to the noun 'al-nās' ('the people'). The article 'al-' loses its 'a' sound after 'li-' and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's initial n (hence the doubled 'nn'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition.
10.root: ن-و-س / ا-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people

11.meaning: 'And as a mercy' — compassion, tenderness, and active kindness shown to others; relief and grace bestowed.
11.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus an indefinite feminine singular noun in the accusative case, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn) on the closed tā'; the accusative often functions adverbially here — '(as) a mercy' — or marks it as a direct object.
11.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tenderness

12.meaning: 'From us' — the preposition 'from' fused with the pronoun 'us,' indicating source or origin in the first-person plural.
12.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / out of') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The nūn of 'min' assimilates into the following 'n', producing the doubled 'minnā.' It marks origin or source: 'from us / on our part.'

13.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

14.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or thing to be done. It can mean an order issued or, more broadly, any business, situation, or decreed affair.
14.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with tanwīn (the -an ending), which marks it as indefinite and typically as the object of a verb ('a matter') or otherwise grammatically governed. The accusative shows it is being acted upon rather than acting.

15.meaning: Decreed, decided, settled, accomplished; a matter that has been firmly determined and brought to completion.
15.grammar: A passive participle on the mafʿīy (مَفۡعِيّ) pattern, which is the form a passive participle takes from a final-weak root — naming the thing that has had the action done to it, here 'something decreed / decided'. The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking an indefinite word in object or descriptive position.
15.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, decide, conclude, carry out; judgement, decree

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she carried/bore', opening with the connective 'so/then'. When used of a woman it commonly means 'she conceived/became pregnant', i.e. she carried a child within her; more broadly the verb covers bearing or carrying any burden or load. The attached 'him' makes the thing carried masculine and singular.
1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The bare verb stem 'ḥamala' is the third-person form; the added '-t' (sukūn-marked tā') signals a feminine singular doer ('she did'). The final '-hu' is an attached object pronoun meaning 'him/it'. The opening 'fa-' joins this to what precedes and often implies sequence or result ('and so').
1.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, conceive, take up a load

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she withdrew / drew herself away / went off to a distant place', opening with 'so/then'. The eighth-form pattern of the root gives the reflexive sense of casting oneself aside, secluding or removing oneself to a remote spot.
2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action in the reflexive/middle (eighth) verb form, which often conveys doing something to or for oneself — here 'casting oneself aside, taking oneself away'. The final '-t' (with sukūn) marks a feminine singular doer ('she'). The opening 'fa-' links it to the preceding clause with a sense of sequence ('and so then').
2.root: ن-ب-ذ (n-b-dh) — to cast aside, throw away, discard

3.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

4.meaning: A place, location, or spot; the position where something is situated.
4.grammar: A noun of place built on the m- pattern (nouns beginning with ma- often denote the place of an action). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, here typically marking 'a place' as the destination or object of a verb of going/taking.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to be

5.meaning: An adjective meaning 'far off, remote, distant' — describing a place set well apart from people and habitation.
5.grammar: An indefinite adjective. The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case with 'a/an' nunation; it typically marks a word as an object, or as describing such a word, and signals indefiniteness ('a remote [place]').
5.root: ق-ص-و (q-ṣ-w) — to be far, distant, remote

1.meaning: A past-tense causative verb meaning 'it brought/drove/compelled her (to come) to', opening with 'then'. The fourth-form pattern makes it causative: to make someone come or to force/drive them to a place. The attached 'her' is the one driven.

parts.en: he/it brought, drove, compelled to come

1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action in the causative (fourth) form ('to make come / drive'). With no separate subject suffix it is third-person masculine singular ('he/it did'). The final '-hā' is an attached object pronoun meaning 'her'. The opening 'fa-' adds the sense of sequence ('then').
1.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive (causative: to bring/drive)

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'the labour/birth-pangs', the onset of childbirth — the contractions and pains by which a child is delivered.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final '-u' ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer of a sentence. The prefix 'al-' makes it definite ('the').
2.root: م-خ-ض (m-kh-ḍ) — to be in labour, the pangs of childbirth

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
3.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'trunk' or 'stem' — the main woody stalk of a tree (especially a palm), or by extension the base/lower part of something.
4.grammar: A noun in the genitive case, shown by the final '-i'. This ending typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF this') or follows a preposition; it marks possession or relationship to what comes before or after.
4.root: ج-ذ-ع (j-dh-ʿ) — trunk, stem of a tree

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'the date-palm', the palm tree that bears dates.
5.grammar: A definite, singular (unit) noun marked feminine by the 'ta' ending. The final '-i' is the genitive case, typically signalling that it follows another noun ('… OF the date-palm') or a preposition. The 'al-' is here pronounced 'an-' because the following 'n' absorbs the 'l' (a sun letter).
5.root: ن-خ-ل (n-kh-l) — date-palm, to sift

6.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.

7.meaning: Oh, would that I…! / I dearly wish that I…; an exclamation of longing and regret, joining a cry of grief to a particle meaning 'if only', with 'I/me' attached — voicing a wish for what is contrary to fact.
7.grammar: An exclamatory particle yā ('O!') plus layta ('if only'), a particle expressing a wish for the impossible or improbable, with the attached pronoun -ī ('me/I'). When a first-person -ī pronoun attaches, a protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) is inserted between the particle and the pronoun — giving -nī — to guard the particle's own final vowel (the fatḥa of layta) from being altered. The -nī here serves as the subject of the wish ('that I…').

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'I died', with the speaker as the one who died. Conveys having passed away, ceased to live.
8.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The '-tu' ending marks a first-person singular doer ('I did'). The hollow root's middle weak letter is dropped and the first vowel shifted, giving 'mittu' rather than a fuller form.
8.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — to die, death

9.meaning: An adverb of time and place meaning 'before' — denoting what comes prior to something else, whether earlier in time or ahead of it in sequence.
9.grammar: An adverb of time/place ending in -a. It is regularly placed before a following noun to mean 'before that thing' (e.g. 'before X'), functioning much like a preposition that the next word completes.
9.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, to come before; the front/fore

10.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
10.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

11.meaning: 'And I was / and I have been' — the conjunction 'and' plus the past-tense verb 'to be' in the first person, used to set a state or describe what one continually was.
11.grammar: Connective 'and' plus the past tense of the verb 'to be'; the '-tu' suffix marks 'I'. It expresses a past or ongoing-past state: 'I was / I used to be'.
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'a thing forgotten', 'oblivion', or 'something cast out of memory' — that which is neglected and not remembered.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case with 'a/an' nunation; it commonly marks an object or a word standing in apposition, and signals indefiniteness ('a forgotten thing').

13.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'forgotten', 'put out of mind' — describing one or that which has been forgotten and left unremembered.
13.grammar: A passive participle (the 'maf'ūl' pattern, 'one that is …-ed'), here meaning 'forgotten'; the full word is 'mansiyy'. The morphological prefix is a plain 'ma-' (single mīm); the doubled mīm sometimes seen in recitation is a sandhi feature where a preceding word's nunation merges into the mīm, not part of the prefix itself. The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case with 'a/an' nunation, typically marking it as an object or describing one, and signalling indefiniteness ('a forgotten one').

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he/it called out to her', opening with 'so/then'. The third-form pattern of the root denotes calling or crying out to someone directly. The attached 'her' is the one called.
1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action in the third verb form (calling out to someone). With no separate subject suffix it is third-person masculine singular ('he/it did'). The final '-hā' is an attached object pronoun meaning 'her'. The opening 'fa-' adds sequence ('and so').
1.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call, cry out, summon

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
3.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

4.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
4.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

5.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'you grieve / feel sorrow', addressed to a single female. It denotes being sad, distressed, or grief-stricken.
5.grammar: An ongoing/future-tense (imperfect) verb. The 'ta-' prefix together with the final '-ī' marks a second-person feminine singular subject ('you', addressing a woman). This same form is commonly used after a prohibition word ('do not …') to tell a woman not to do something.
5.root: ح-ز-ن (ḥ-z-n) — grief, sorrow, sadness

6.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

7.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint

8.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a female). Rabb is the Lord, Master, and Sustainer — owner, nurturer, governor, and the one who brings each thing to completion. The attached pronoun makes it 'your', addressed to a single female.
8.grammar: The stem rabb carries the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks the word as the subject — the one performing the action or being spoken about ('your Lord [says/does]…'). The final -ki is the attached possessive pronoun 'your', addressing a single female (contrast -ka for a male).
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

9.meaning: A location word meaning 'beneath you / under you', addressed to a single female. 'Taḥt' means 'under, below, beneath', and the attached 'you' specifies the person below whom something lies.
9.grammar: An adverb of place ('under/beneath') with an attached possessive-type pronoun. The ending '-ki' (with kasra) is the second-person feminine singular pronoun, addressing a woman ('you'). Such place-words are grammatically in the accusative as adverbs of location.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'a small stream/rivulet' of running water; some also relate it to one who is noble or eminent. In the sense of water it is a flowing brook or channel.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case with 'a/an' nunation, which typically marks an object and signals indefiniteness ('a stream').
10.root: س-ر-ي (s-r-y) — to flow/travel by night; (relatedly) nobility

1.meaning: A command meaning 'shake / jolt / cause to sway', addressed to a single female, opening with 'and'. It is an order to give something a shaking or tugging motion.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The final '-ī' marks it as addressed to a single female ('you [woman], do it!'). The doubled middle letter (shadda) belongs to this root's pattern. The opening 'wa-' simply means 'and'.
1.root: ه-ز-ز (h-z-z) — to shake, jolt, convulse

2.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'towards you / to you', addressed to a single female. 'Ilā' means 'to, toward', expressing direction or motion toward something; the attached 'you' is the goal.
2.grammar: A preposition of direction ('to/toward') with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā' shifts to 'ilay-' before a suffix. The ending '-ki' (with kasra) is the second-person feminine singular pronoun ('you', addressing a woman), which is the object of the preposition.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'trunk/stem' preceded by 'with / by means of'. 'Jidhʿ' is the woody trunk of a tree (especially a palm); the prefixed 'bi-' adds the sense 'with / by / by means of'.
3.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with/by'). Any noun after this preposition takes the genitive case, shown here by the final '-i'. The phrase as a whole means 'with/by the trunk'.
3.root: ج-ذ-ع (j-dh-ʿ) — trunk, stem of a tree

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'the date-palm', the palm tree that bears dates.
4.grammar: A definite, singular (unit) noun marked feminine by the 'ta' ending. The final '-i' is the genitive case, typically signalling that it follows another noun ('… OF the date-palm') or a preposition. The 'al-' is here pronounced 'an-' because the following 'n' absorbs the 'l' (a sun letter).

5.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'it lets fall, makes drop, sheds (in succession)'. The form conveys the fruit being dropped piece by piece, in successive or repeated falls.
5.grammar: An ongoing/future-tense (imperfect) verb in the third (mufāʿala) form, whose sense here is successive or gradual dropping (letting things fall one after another), not a causative-intensive (that is the second form). The 'tu-' prefix marks a third-person feminine singular (or second-person masculine) subject ('it/she …'). The final consonant carries a sukūn (no vowel), the jussive/short form often used after conditional or command-linked particles.
5.root: س-ق-ط (s-q-ṭ) — to fall, drop down

6.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'upon you / on you / over you', addressed to a single female. 'ʿalā' means 'on, upon, over'; the attached 'you' is the one upon whom something rests or falls.
6.grammar: A preposition ('on/upon') with an attached pronoun. The base 'ʿalā' shifts to 'ʿalay-' before a suffix. The ending '-ki' (with kasra) is the second-person feminine singular pronoun ('you', addressing a woman), the object of the preposition.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'fresh, ripe, moist dates' — dates at the soft, juicy stage, ready to eat.
7.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case with nunation, typically marking the word as an object ('[drops] fresh dates') and signalling indefiniteness ('some fresh dates').
7.root: ر-ط-ب (r-ṭ-b) — to be moist, fresh, ripe

8.meaning: An adjective meaning 'freshly picked, just-gathered, ripe' — describing fruit newly plucked and ready.
8.grammar: An indefinite adjective. The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case with nunation; it agrees with and describes an accusative noun ('fresh dates, newly gathered') and signals indefiniteness.
8.root: ج-ن-ي (j-n-y) — to gather/pluck (fruit)

1.meaning: A command meaning 'eat!', addressed to a single female, opening with 'so/then'. A direct order to consume food.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The final '-ī' marks it as addressed to a single female ('you [woman], eat!'). The bare stem 'kul' is the shortened command form of this weak-first-letter root. The opening 'fa-' means 'so/then'.
1.root: أ-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat, consume

2.meaning: A command meaning 'drink!', addressed to a single female, opening with 'and'. A direct order to drink.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the word begin (a 'connecting hamza'). The final '-ī' marks it as addressed to a single female ('you [woman], drink!'). The opening 'wa-' means 'and'.

3.meaning: A command meaning 'be glad / be comforted / let (your eye) be cooled', addressed to a single female, opening with 'and'. The idiom 'cool the eye' means to be reassured, content, and joyful — relief from anxious tears.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The doubled final letter (shadda) belongs to this root's pattern. The final '-ī' marks it as addressed to a single female ('you [woman], do it!'). The opening 'wa-' means 'and'. It is typically paired with the word 'eye' to form the idiom 'cool your eye' = 'be glad/comforted'.
3.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — to be cool, settled, at rest (idiom: contentment of the eye)

4.meaning: 'A spring / a flowing fountain (of water)'. The noun ʿayn carries several senses — an eye, a flowing spring, the essence of a thing — and in the watery sense it means a gushing source or fountain.
4.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative; after a number such as 'twelve', the counted thing takes exactly this singular accusative form ('twelve spring' in Arabic idiom). The nunation also conveys 'a' (unspecified).

5.meaning: A compound conditional expression meaning 'then if ever' or 'so whenever'. It combines 'then/so' with a conditional 'if' to introduce a case that may arise, usually paired with a following emphasis on the verb.
5.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so') joined to immā, itself the conditional particle 'in' ('if') merged with an emphasising mā. It sets up a condition — 'if it should happen that…' — and characteristically leads to a verb reinforced with a strong 'certainly' ending.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (feminine singular) will surely see, perceive, or notice (someone or something).' It carries an emphatic force: the doubled 'n' ending stresses the certainty or insistence of the seeing, as in 'you will most certainly see.'
6.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'); combined with the feminine-singular shape it addresses a single woman. The doubled -nna is the heavy emphatic suffix (nun al-tawkid), which intensifies the verb into 'you will surely / definitely see.'
6.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, to perceive, to behold

7.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

8.meaning: 'Humankind, human beings, mortals.' A collective noun for humanity as flesh-and-blood creatures, often emphasizing the physical, mortal nature of people as distinct from angels or the divine.
8.grammar: A definite noun with the prefixed article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or as governed by a preposition or oath particle.
8.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — human skin, and by extension humankind; also good news

9.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

10.meaning: 'Then say!' / 'So say!' — a command addressed to a single female to utter or speak something. The attached 'then/so' links the speaking to what precedes as a consequence.
10.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The fa- prefix means 'then' or 'so,' connecting it to a prior statement. The -i ending is the feminine-singular imperative marker, directing the order specifically to one woman.
10.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

11.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
11.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

12.meaning: I vowed, I pledged, I dedicated — the past-tense verb 'to make a vow', committing oneself (or dedicating something) to Allah by a solemn promise.
12.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing completed action. The -tu ending marks a first-person singular subject — 'I (did it)'. The verb conveys binding oneself by a vow or consecrating something to Allah.
12.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to vow, pledge, dedicate; also to warn

13.meaning: 'To / for the All-Merciful.' Al-Rahman is a divine name of Allah denoting the One whose mercy is vast, all-embracing, and overflowing to the whole of creation; the prefixed 'to/for' directs an action or dedication toward Him.
13.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('to / for'). Because li- demands the genitive case, the noun takes the final -i ending. The article al- assimilates into the following 'r' sound (heard as ar-Rahman). The form al-Rahman is an intensive pattern signifying overwhelming, all-encompassing mercy.

14.meaning: 'A fast / fasting' — abstinence; in religious usage, the disciplined withholding from food, drink, speech, or other things as an act of devotion.
14.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (with tanwin) is accusative and indefinite ('a fast'); the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb or the thing vowed/specified.
14.root: ص-و-م (ṣ-w-m) — to abstain, to fast, to hold back

15.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.

16.meaning: '(That) I speak / I should speak' — a first-person verb meaning to talk to or address someone, conveying speech as an act of conversation directed at another.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb in Form II (the doubled middle 'l' gives a sense of speaking directly to or addressing someone). The u- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -a ending is subjunctive, the mood used after particles meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or 'in order to.'

17.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
17.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
17.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

18.meaning: 'A human / a human being, a mortal man' — denotes a member of humankind, one of mankind, especially as a single individual person.
18.grammar: An indefinite noun (a relational/adjectival form from the word for 'mankind'). The -an ending (with tanwin) is accusative and indefinite; the accusative often marks a direct object or, after a negation, the thing being denied ('any human').

1.meaning: 'Then she came / so she brought (it).' A past-tense verb of a single female arriving or coming, with an attached 'then/so' linking the arrival to what came before.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The fa- prefix means 'then' or 'so,' marking sequence or result. The final -t ending is the feminine-singular marker, showing the subject is 'she' (one female).
1.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to bring

2.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

3.meaning: 'Her people / her folk' — one's own community, kinsfolk, or nation; the group of people to whom one belongs. With the attached pronoun it means 'her people.'
3.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -ha suffix means 'her,' showing possession ('her people'). The -a vowel before it is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object of a verb (e.g., the destination one comes to).
3.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people standing together as a community

4.meaning: 'She is carrying him / bearing him' — a present-tense verb of carrying, bearing, or holding something, with an attached 'him' as the thing carried.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The ta- prefix here marks a third-person feminine-singular subject ('she'). The -u ending is indicative, the mood for a plain, ongoing or habitual action. The -hu suffix is the object 'him / it.'
4.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, to bear, to bear a burden or load

5.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

6.meaning: A call meaning 'O Maryam' (Mary) — the vocative particle yā ('O') used to address or summon, attached to the proper name Maryam.
6.grammar: A direct address: the particle yā ('O') is used to call out to someone, followed by the name Maryam. The final -u ending is the standard form a singular name takes when being called.

7.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
7.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

8.meaning: 'You (feminine singular) have come / have brought (something).' A past-tense verb of coming or bringing, addressed to one woman.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ti ending is the second-person feminine-singular subject marker, meaning 'you' addressed to a single female who performed the act ('you have come/brought').
8.root: ج-ي-أ (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive, to bring forth

9.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

10.meaning: 'An unheard-of, outrageous, or monstrous thing' — something strange, unprecedented, and shockingly extraordinary; a deed so novel it provokes astonishment or disapproval.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on an intensive pattern. The -an ending (with tanwin) is accusative and indefinite ('an unheard-of thing'); the accusative commonly marks the direct object of a verb such as 'to bring' or 'to do.'
10.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to cut/split; to fabricate or invent, hence something startlingly novel

1.meaning: 'O sister!' — a call or address to a female sibling; by extension a woman likened or affiliated to a family, group, or lineage ('sister of …').
1.grammar: A noun preceded by the vocative particle ya ('O'), used to call or address someone. The -a ending appears because a called noun that is joined to a following word (as in 'O sister of …') takes the accusative case.
1.root: أ-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brotherhood/sisterhood, sibling, kinship

2.meaning: Aaron, the proper name of the brother of Moses, a prophet of Allah.
2.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign/non-Arabic name, it is a 'diptote': it refuses the usual -i for the genitive and instead shows -a, and it never takes nunation. The -a ending here stands in for the genitive, the case used after a preceding noun ('… OF Aaron') or after a preposition.

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

4.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

5.meaning: 'Your father' — one's male parent. With the attached pronoun it means 'your (feminine singular) father.'
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. 'Father' is one of a small set of nouns that show case with a long vowel; the -u here signals the nominative (the role of subject or the one being described). The -ki suffix means 'your,' addressed to a single female.
5.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — father, fatherhood

6.meaning: 'A man, a person' — an individual human being, typically a man. Often paired with a following descriptive noun to characterize the kind of person ('a man of …').
6.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) hamza and ending in a hamza root letter. The final -a is accusative, the case that commonly marks a direct object or a noun that is being predicated/described (e.g., 'he was not a man of …').
6.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — manliness, a human individual; related to 'manly vigor'

7.meaning: 'Evil, badness, wickedness' — that which is bad, harmful, or wrong; often used in a possessive link ('a man of evil,' i.e., a wicked or immoral person).
7.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -in ending (with tanwin) is genitive and indefinite; the genitive typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive sense ('a man OF evil') or follows a preposition.
7.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — evil, badness, to do wrong, to grieve

8.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
8.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
9.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: 'Your mother' — one's female parent. With the attached pronoun it means 'your (feminine singular) mother.'
10.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before the suffix is nominative, the case marking a subject or the thing being described. The -ki suffix means 'your,' addressed to a single female.
10.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — source/origin, mother; relates to 'community' and 'foundation'

11.meaning: An unchaste woman; one who transgresses sexual bounds. The root sense is overstepping limits and rebellion, applied here to immoral, licentious conduct.
11.grammar: A noun/adjective on the faʿīl pattern conveying an ingrained quality. The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking it as indefinite and in object or predicate position ('[I have not been] an unchaste woman').
11.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to exceed bounds, transgress, act wrongfully; sexual immorality

1.meaning: 'Then she pointed / gestured / indicated.' A past-tense verb of pointing or signaling toward something, with an attached 'then/so' marking sequence.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form IV (a pattern that here means to make a sign or gesture). The fa- prefix means 'then' or 'so.' The final -t ending is the feminine-singular marker, showing the subject is 'she' (one female).
1.root: ش-و-ر (sh-w-r) — to indicate, to point out, to signal; also to consult

2.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

3.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

4.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
4.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

5.meaning: '(How) can we speak / shall we speak' — a first-person plural verb meaning to talk to or address someone, expressed as 'we.'
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in Form II (the doubled middle 'l' conveys speaking directly to or addressing someone). The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The -u ending is indicative, the mood for a plain statement or question about an action.
5.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — speech, word, to speak

6.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
6.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

7.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

7.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
8.root: — (particle)

9.meaning: 'The cradle' — the infant's crib or rocking-bed; by extension, the state of earliest infancy. It denotes the resting place prepared for a newborn.
9.grammar: A definite noun with the al- prefix ('the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'). The noun is on the faʿl pattern (mahd), a simple verbal-noun form derived from the act of smoothing/preparing a bed.
9.root: م-ه-د (m-h-d) — to spread out, smooth, prepare (a bed/resting place)

10.meaning: A child, young boy, or infant — a male in early childhood. The word denotes someone of tender, pre-adult age.
10.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern. The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — it often marks a circumstantial state ('while [still] a child') or a direct object, and the nunation shows indefiniteness.
10.root: ص-ب-و / ص-ب-ي (ṣ-b-w/y) — childhood, to be young/inclined

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: 'A servant / bondsman of Allah' — one who worships and is wholly owned by and devoted to Allah; the word denotes humble servanthood and total dependence on the Master.
3.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the noun used to identify/describe someone ('I am a servant'). It frequently stands at the head of a possessive link, as in 'servant of …'.
3.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve; servitude and devotion

4.meaning: The proper name of the One True God in Arabic, Allāh — the unique, absolute Divine Being, alone worthy of worship. Used by Arabic-speaking Muslims, Christians, and Jews for the one Creator and Lord of all.
4.grammar: The proper divine name. The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links this name to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of Allah / belonging to Allah' relationship.

5.meaning: 'He gave me / He granted me' — a past-tense verb of giving or bestowing, with Allah commonly the implied giver, and an attached 'me' as the recipient.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form IV ('to give, to grant'). With no added subject marker it is third-person masculine singular ('he gave'). The -ni/-ya suffix is the object 'me,' so the whole means 'He gave me.'
5.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this stem, to bring to / to give, to bestow

6.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
6.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

7.meaning: And He made me / placed me — to set, render, or appoint someone into a particular state or rank; 'and He caused me to be…'.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb led by wa- ('and'). The -a marks the doer as a single male ('he'), and the attached -nī is the object 'me', so it reads 'and he made/placed me'. The verb often takes a second word naming the state into which someone or something is set.
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to place, to render

8.meaning: 'A prophet' — one whom Allah inspires and sends with revelation to guide people; a bearer of divine news and message.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (with tanwin) is accusative and indefinite ('a prophet'); the accusative commonly marks the object of making/appointing or a predicate after certain verbs ('He made [me] a prophet').
8.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; one who brings news (a prophet)

1.meaning: 'And He made me / and He appointed me / and He rendered me (such-and-such).' A past-tense verb of making, placing, or appointing, with an attached 'me' and a leading 'and.'
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The wa- prefix means 'and,' joining it to what precedes. With no added subject marker the verb is third-person masculine singular ('he made'). The -ni suffix is the object 'me,' giving 'He made me.'
1.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to render, to place, to appoint

2.meaning: Blessed — filled with and a source of divine blessing (baraka), abounding in good that increases and endures.
2.grammar: A passive participle (something that has been blessed) used as a descriptive word. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks a word functioning as an object or as a descriptive 'state', and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a blessed thing').

3.meaning: Where / wherever. An interrogative or conditional adverb of place: it asks 'where?' or, in a conditional sense, sets up 'wherever / in whatever place'.
3.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of place fixed on a final -a; it does not change for case. It functions either as a question word ('where?') or as a conditional particle introducing a clause ('wherever'), often pairing with a following verb in the jussive mood.

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: 'I was / I have been' — a first-person past form of the verb 'to be,' indicating a state or condition one was in.
5.grammar: A past-tense form of the verb 'to be' (a hollow verb whose middle root letter drops in this form). The -tu ending is the first-person-singular subject marker, meaning 'I' ('I was'). It often introduces a description of one's former state, frequently followed by a noun or adjective in the accusative.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come into being

6.meaning: And He has charged/enjoined me — i.e. laid an obligation or solemn instruction upon me. The verb conveys giving a firm directive or binding counsel that one is expected to keep.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'he' form (third-person masculine singular), prefixed with wa- ('and'). The attached -nī ending is the object 'me' (the n is a connecting consonant that regularly appears before this pronoun on verbs). So the form reads literally 'and he enjoined me.'
6.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to enjoin, instruct, bequeath, give binding counsel

7.meaning: With/by the ritual prayer — the formal act of worship (ṣalāh) involving prescribed standing, bowing, and prostration. The term denotes devotional prayer as an instituted observance, distinct from informal supplication.
7.grammar: A feminine noun carrying 'the' (al-), governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -i is the genitive case, which is exactly what a noun takes after a preposition like bi-; the genitive also typically signals an 'of' relationship to a preceding word.
7.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — ritual prayer, worship; connection/devotion

8.meaning: And the obligatory almsgiving (zakāh) — the prescribed portion of one's wealth given to purify it and aid those in need. The word carries the sense of purification and growth as well as the alms themselves.
8.grammar: A feminine noun with 'the' (al-) and the conjunction wa- ('and'). The final -i is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when joined to a preceding genitive noun (it commonly carries an 'of' sense).
8.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure, to grow; purification, almsgiving

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: 'I remained / I continued / as long as I stayed' — first-person past of a verb meaning to persist or go on being in a state; often used with the sense 'so long as I was …'.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-tu' suffix marking 'I'. It denotes continuing or persisting in a state, frequently introducing a 'for as long as I remained …' clause.
10.root: د-و-م (d-w-m) — to last, endure, continue, persist

11.meaning: Living, alive — describing someone or something possessing life. As an adjective it characterizes a being in the state of life.
11.grammar: A singular masculine adjective in the indefinite accusative case, shown by the -an ending (the tanwīn). This ending commonly marks a word as a descriptive complement or 'state' — telling in what condition something is (e.g. '… while alive').
11.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, to live, to be alive

1.meaning: Dutiful, kind, and devoted — especially toward one's parents. The word describes someone abundant in goodness, devotion, and benevolent treatment of others; it can also mean truly righteous and pious.
1.grammar: An adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) on the pattern faʿl, with the final root letter doubled (ب-ر-ر → بَرّ). The '-an' ending (an 'a' vowel with nunation 'n') is accusative and indefinite — it commonly marks a descriptive complement or predicate, and the nunation shows it is indefinite. The leading 'wa' means 'and.'
1.root: ب-ر-ر (b-r-r) — to be dutiful, devoted, abundantly good

2.meaning: To my mother — the female parent. The word denotes specifically 'mother' (one who gives birth) rather than the more general term for parent, and here it carries the preposition 'to/with' and the possessive 'my.'
2.grammar: A feminine noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/to') and carrying the possessive 'my' (-ī) at the end. There is no conjunction here: the opening bi- is the preposition, not 'and.' Because the noun follows a preposition and bears an attached pronoun, it stands in the genitive; the -ī suffix means 'my,' so the whole reads 'to/with my mother.'
2.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth; child, parent, offspring

3.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
3.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

4.meaning: He makes/renders me — to set, appoint, or cause someone to become something. The verb can mean 'to make' in the sense of fashioning, or 'to render/turn into' a particular state.
4.grammar: An imperfect verb in the 'he' form: the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The stem ends in sukūn (jʿal, not jʿalu), so the verb is in the jussive/apocopate mood — the vowel-less ending produced by a preceding particle or conditional context, not the plain indicative. The attached -nī is the object 'me' (with the connecting n). So it reads 'he makes/renders me.'
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, appoint, render

5.meaning: A tyrant; an overbearing, domineering person who forces his will on others, haughty and merciless. The pattern is intensive, conveying someone whose oppressive power is a defining trait. When used of Allah, the same root word means the All-Compeller, but in human reference it is blameworthy arrogance.
5.grammar: This is a noun on the intensive pattern faʿʿāl, which marks an ingrained or habitual quality ('one who constantly compels/oppresses'). The final -an (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending: it marks the word as 'a tyrant' (indefinite) and signals it is functioning as an object or predicate rather than a subject.
5.root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r) — to compel, force, restore by force; might, dominance

6.meaning: Wretched, miserable, ill-fated, deprived of good; one who fails or is left disappointed. The opposite of blessed and successful.
6.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation, indefinite. In this case it commonly serves as a predicate-complement of certain verbs ('was/became wretched') or describes an accusative noun; the nunation marks it indefinite.
6.root: ش-ق-و / ش-ق-ي (sh-q-w / sh-q-y) — to be wretched, suffer hardship

1.meaning: And peace — wholeness, safety, and freedom from harm. As a noun it denotes the state and the greeting of peace, security, and well-being.
1.grammar: A masculine noun with 'the' (al-) and the conjunction wa- ('and'). The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject or as the starting topic of a statement ('peace is/be …').
1.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, safety, peace, submission

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'upon / on / over' fused with the attached pronoun 'me,' giving 'upon me / against me / on my account.' The base preposition signals being on top of, responsible for, or burdened by something, and can also carry the sense of something owed by or weighing against a person.
2.grammar: A preposition with the first-person singular pronoun 'me' attached. When the pronoun 'me' joins this preposition, its form shifts so the two merge into 'ʿalayya.' Pronouns attached to prepositions always take the object form ('me,' not 'I'), and no case ending applies to them.

3.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
3.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

4.meaning: I was born — to be brought into the world by birth. This is the passive of the verb 'to give birth,' so the subject is the one born rather than the one giving birth.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The internal vowel pattern wu-i marks it as passive ('was/were …ed'), and the suffix -tu is the subject 'I.' Together: 'I was born.'
4.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth; child, offspring

5.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

6.meaning: I die / I will die — to undergo death, the ending of life. The verb expresses the act of dying as it happens to the subject.
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the 'I' form: the a- prefix marks the first-person singular ('I …'). The final -u is the indicative ending, which marks a plain, ongoing or future statement of fact (not a command or a negated/subordinate form).

7.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

8.meaning: I am raised up / I will be brought back to life — to be resurrected, sent forth, or roused. In the passive it conveys being raised from death or being dispatched.
8.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb in the 'I' form. The u- prefix (with the a-vowel on the stem) marks first-person singular passive — 'I am being …ed.' The final -u is the indicative ending of a plain statement. So: 'I am/will be raised up.'
8.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send, raise up, resurrect, rouse

9.meaning: Living / alive: possessing life, animate and vital, not dead or inert.
9.grammar: An adjective. The final -an (accusative with tanwīn) is indefinite and typically marks it as a descriptive complement or as the object/state of a verb (e.g. describing how or what something is).

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: "Isa" — the personal name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary.
2.grammar: A proper name (a foreign/non-Arabic name). It is fully indeclinable: its ending does not change for case, so it stays the same as subject, object, or after a preposition.

3.meaning: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
3.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
3.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

4.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
4.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

5.meaning: The saying, statement, or utterance — speech that is spoken; a word, remark, or what someone says.
5.grammar: A noun, 'saying/speech.' The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object — the thing the verb acts upon (e.g., what is heard, said, or known). This form names the act or product of speaking.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; an utterance

6.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
6.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

7.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

8.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

9.meaning: A present/ongoing verb meaning '(they) doubt / dispute / are in uncertainty.' Built on a reflexive stem, it conveys harboring or trading in doubt and wrangling over something.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in a reflexive (Form VIII) pattern. The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' acting in the ongoing/indicative mood. The sense is 'they keep doubting / disputing'.

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: That he take/adopt — to take for oneself, acquire, or adopt. This verb form (reflexive 'take to oneself') often carries the sense of taking something as one's own, e.g. adopting or claiming.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the 'he' form (ya- prefix). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that / so that / to,' giving the sense 'that he should take' or 'for him to take.'
5.root: ا-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, acquire

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: A child / a son / offspring — a son or, more broadly, offspring born to someone. The word denotes a born child without itself specifying gender, though it is often rendered 'son.'
7.grammar: A masculine noun in the indefinite accusative case, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). It is accusative because it serves as the direct object of the verb 'to take/adopt' — the thing taken. The opening wa- here is the first root letter of the word (wa-lad), not the conjunction 'and.' Indefinite -an gives the sense 'a child / any child.'
7.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth; child, offspring

8.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
8.grammar: A verbal noun used as an absolute exclamation, fixed in the accusative ending -a (an emphatic declaration, roughly 'I declare His utter transcendence'). The attached -hu is the possessive/object pronoun 'Him', referring to one masculine person.
8.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide away, hence to declare Allah free of all imperfection
