9.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

10.meaning: To decree, determine, settle, or carry out conclusively — to bring a matter to its final, binding completion, whether by judging, ordaining, or accomplishing it.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he decreed/settled.' The bare stem ending in a long final vowel marks a completed action done by one male. With no extra subject suffix, the doer is simply 'he'.
10.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decide conclusively, decree, complete

11.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or thing to be done. It can mean an order issued or, more broadly, any business, situation, or decreed affair.
11.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with tanwīn (the -an ending), which marks it as indefinite and typically as the object of a verb ('a matter') or otherwise grammatically governed. The accusative shows it is being acted upon rather than acting.
11.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also affair/matter

12.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
12.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

13.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
13.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

14.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
14.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

15.meaning: The command 'Be!' — an order to come into existence, the creative imperative by which a thing is summoned into being.
15.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'Be!' It is the shortened command form of the verb 'to be/become,' with the bare, vowel-less ending typical of a singular order.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

16.meaning: 'And it comes to be / and it is' — the act of existence following upon a command, expressing that something duly comes into being.
16.grammar: The connector 'fa-' ('so/and then') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is/becomes'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking an ordinary, unconditioned present or future statement; the doer 'it/he' is built into the verb.
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

1.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

4.meaning: 'And your Lord' (Lord of a group) — joining the speaker's Lord to that of the addressees: the one Master and Sustainer of both.
4.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The noun rabb shows an -u vowel, the nominative case typically marking the subject or predicate of a sentence ('… IS the Lord'). The ending -kum is the possessive pronoun for a group ('your', masculine/mixed plural).
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: 'So worship Him' — a directive to a group to serve, devote themselves to, and humbly submit in worship to Him.
5.grammar: fa- is a connector meaning 'so' or 'then', often drawing a consequence. The stem is a command (imperative) verb; the -ū ending addresses a masculine/mixed plural ('you all do it'). The final -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it', so the whole means 'so worship Him'.
5.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, to devote oneself

6.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
6.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

7.meaning: 'A path / a road / a way' — a clear traveled route; used figuratively for a way of life or course of conduct.
7.grammar: The noun ṣirāṭ ('path'). The ending -un (nunation with -u) marks it as indefinite ('a path') and in the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate ('… IS a path').
7.root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ) — a way, road, or path

8.meaning: 'Straight / upright / direct' — describing something perfectly even and undeviating, leading directly to its goal without crookedness.
8.grammar: An active participle of the form mustafʿil (here mustaqīm, 'one that is standing straight / upright'), built from the Form X verb istafʿala (here istaqāma, 'to stand straight, be upright'). It functions as an adjective. The ending -un marks it as indefinite and nominative, the case that typically matches a described subject or predicate ('a … one that is straight').
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to be upright/straight

1.meaning: Then they differed / fell into disagreement — to diverge, dispute, or hold conflicting views. The verb conveys parties coming to differ among themselves, often into opposing factions.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'he/they' form (third-person masculine; with a plural subject it reads 'they differed'). The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' marking sequence or consequence. The verb's reflexive pattern (ikht-) gives the mutual sense 'differed among one another.'
1.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after / be different; succession, disagreement

2.meaning: The factions / parties / confederates — groups banded together, especially partisan groups or sects who align as a bloc.
2.grammar: A plural noun (singular ḥizb, 'party/faction') with 'the' (al-). The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a verb ('the factions [did] …').

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: Among them / between them — the relational word 'between/among' combined with 'them.' It marks something occurring in the space, relationship, or midst shared by a group.
4.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'between/among,' carrying the attached pronoun -him ('them,' masculine plural). It sits in the genitive (-i before the pronoun), as such adverb-like nouns regularly do; the whole means 'among/between them.'

5.meaning: 'So woe …' — a connective 'so/then' plus 'woe': an exclamation of impending doom, ruin, or grievous distress called down upon someone. It is a cry of warning and lament, not a literal noun of place.
5.grammar: The connective fa- ('so / then') prefixed to the noun 'woe.' The noun stands in the nominative with indefinite marking (the -un ending, tanwīn). Used this way it functions as an exclamation — 'woe (be) to …' — typically followed by 'to/for' someone.
5.root: و-ي-ل (w-y-l) — woe; ruin, doom, grievous distress

6.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

7.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: A witnessing / a scene / an appointed place or time of gathering — the noun denotes either the act of witnessing, or the place/occasion where people are present and assembled. It derives from the verb 'to witness / be present.'
9.grammar: A noun of place/time/occasion formed on the ma- pattern (a 'place or occasion of witnessing'). The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of …' relationship to a preceding noun.
9.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, be present, testify

10.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
10.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

11.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
11.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
11.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: How well they hear! — an exclamation of wonder at the keenness of hearing. This fixed exclamatory verb form expresses amazement, roughly 'how (acutely) they will hear!'
1.grammar: A fixed exclamatory verb form (the 'afʿil!' pattern of wonder). Though shaped like a command, it functions as an exclamation of astonishment — 'how clearly/acutely they hear!' — and stays in this invariable form.
1.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen

2.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
2.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

3.meaning: And how well they see! — an exclamation marveling at the sharpness of sight, parallel to the exclamation of hearing: 'and how (clearly) they will see!'
3.grammar: A fixed exclamatory verb form (the 'afʿil!' pattern of wonder), joined by wa- ('and'). Though shaped like a command, it expresses amazement — 'how clearly they see!' — and remains in this invariable form.

4.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
4.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

5.meaning: They come to us — to arrive at or approach the speaker's group. The verb 'to come' here carries the object 'us' as the destination of the coming.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the 'they' form: the ya- prefix plus the -ūna ending marks third-person masculine plural ('they …'). The -ūna form (with the final nūn intact) is the indicative of a plain statement. The attached -nā is the object 'us.' So: 'they come to us.'
5.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

6.meaning: But, however, rather — a particle that sets off a correction or contrast with what came before, redirecting the statement.

parts.en: kasra of the light (reduced) particle form

6.grammar: A contrastive particle meaning 'but/however'. This is the light/reduced form of the emphatic لٰكِنَّ (lākinna): the doubled nūn is elided and the particle no longer governs a following noun. The final kasra (-i) belongs to the identity of this reduced form rather than being mere pronunciation liaison.

7.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
7.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression

8.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
8.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
8.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
10.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

11.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
11.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
11.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: And warn them — to caution, alert to danger, or give solemn notice of a coming consequence. The verb means to put someone on guard against something feared.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to 'you' (masculine singular), meaning 'warn!', joined by wa- ('and') and carrying the object -hum ('them'). Its clipped, vowel-less ending is typical of the command form. So: 'and warn them.'
1.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice

2.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
2.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
2.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

3.meaning: The regret / anguished remorse — deep grief and bitter sorrow over what has been lost or missed, the painful wishing that one had acted otherwise.
3.grammar: A feminine noun with 'the' (al-). The final -i is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or in an 'of …' relationship to a preceding noun (e.g. 'the day of regret').
3.root: ح-س-ر (ḥ-s-r) — to grieve, regret; to be exhausted/laid bare

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

5.meaning: It was decided, decreed, or settled — a matter brought to a final verdict and concluded; to be judged and disposed of with finality.
5.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, 'it was decreed/judged' — the vowel pattern qu-i marks it as passive (done to an unnamed subject rather than by a stated doer). Its root ends in a weak letter, which here appears as final -ya; the form is third-person masculine singular ('it was settled / the matter was concluded').
5.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — deciding, decreeing, settling

6.meaning: The matter, affair, or command; a thing decided upon or ordered, or a situation/business at hand. It can denote both a "command" and an "affair" depending on usage.
6.grammar: A definite noun with prefixed al- ("the"). The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as the thing an action is predicated of.

7.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
7.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
8.root: — (particle)

9.meaning: Heedlessness / inattention — a state of being unaware, distracted, or oblivious; failing to take notice of what matters.
9.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite genitive case, marked by the -in ending (tanwīn on the feminine -t-). The genitive is the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of …' relationship; indefinite -in gives the sense 'a state of heedlessness.'
9.root: غ-ف-ل (gh-f-l) — to be heedless, neglectful, unaware

10.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
10.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.
10.root: — (conjunction plus pronoun; no root)

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
2.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

3.meaning: We inherit / We give as inheritance — to receive, take over, or pass on what remains after another. The verb conveys succeeding to possession of what is left behind.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the 'we' form: the na- prefix marks the first-person plural ('we …'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of ongoing or future fact. So: 'we inherit.'
3.root: و-ر-ث (w-r-th) — to inherit, succeed to, pass on as heritage

4.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

5.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
5.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
5.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
6.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

7.meaning: And to us / and unto us — the directional word 'to/toward' combined with 'us,' marking the speaker's group as the destination, goal, or point of return.
7.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun is attached, joined here with -nā ('us') and prefixed by wa- ('and'). It marks direction or destination — 'and to us / and unto us.'
7.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: They are made to go back / they are returned — a passive verb meaning a group is caused to return or be brought back to a starting point or to the One who originated them.
8.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb in the passive voice: the 'yu-' prefix combined with the 'a' vowel on the middle root letter (yuC-CaCu) signals that the subject undergoes the action rather than doing it ('they are returned', not 'they return'). The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') and the indicative mood, used for ongoing or future action.
8.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, revert

1.meaning: 'And mention / and remember / and recall' — a command to bring something to mind and call it out, whether by remembering it inwardly or speaking of it aloud.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- is 'and'. The stem is a command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'mention / remember!'. The helping vowel at the start (the alif pronounced u-) is needed to begin the word, and the final consonant carries a vowelless ending (sukūn), which is the typical close of a singular command.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind; remembrance

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
3.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

4.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (Abraham), the patriarch and prophet.
4.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Its ending '-a' reflects that it is 'diptote' — a noun that does not take the usual indefinite 'n' sound and uses '-a' for both the accusative and the genitive. Here the '-a' serves the genitive role, linking it to a preceding noun ('… of Ibrāhīm').

5.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
5.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

6.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

6.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

7.meaning: An utterly truthful one — a person of intense, habitual truthfulness who both speaks truth and lives by it, and unhesitatingly affirms the truth of what is revealed. An emphatic, saint-like degree of sincerity.
7.grammar: A noun in an intensive pattern (fiʿʿīl, with an initial kasra: ṣi-) that conveys an extreme or constant quality. The '-an' ending (with tanwīn, the doubled 'n' sound) marks it as indefinite ('a truthful one') and in the accusative case, the case typically used for objects of verbs and for predicates after certain verbs.
7.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

8.meaning: A prophet — one who receives revelation from Allah and conveys news and guidance from Him to people.
8.grammar: A noun (pattern faʿīl). In isolation it is نَبِيّ (nabiyy): a single nūn, then a doubled final 'yy' (shadda on the yāʾ) that belongs to the word. The '-an' ending (tanwīn, the doubled 'n' sound) marks it as indefinite ('a prophet') and in the accusative case — the case used for objects and predicates.
8.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to inform, announce

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: To / for his father — the noun 'father' attached to a possessive 'his' and preceded by the preposition 'to/for.'
3.grammar: Preposition + noun + possessive pronoun. The li- prefix means 'to' or 'for.' 'Father' is one of a small group of nouns that show case with a long vowel: the -ī here reflects the genitive required after the preposition. The attached -hi means 'his' (its 'i' vowel harmonizes after the preceding -ī).

4.meaning: An affectionate vocative meaning 'O my father' — a tender form of address to one's father, where the original possessive 'my' is replaced by a final -i that carries the same intimate sense.
4.grammar: A vocative: the particle 'yā' is used to call or address someone. The ending -ati (with its final -i) is a special endearing form used when addressing one's father; the -i here stands in for the dropped possessive pronoun 'my', so the whole means 'O my father'.

5.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
5.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

6.meaning: You worship / you serve — to direct devotion, obedience, and submission toward something as an object of worship.
6.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, used for plain statements of ongoing or future action ('you worship').
6.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit in devotion

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: 'He/it hears / listens.' To perceive sound with the ear; by extension, to heed or pay attention to what is said.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a single masculine doer, 'he/it [does/is doing].' The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement.

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: He sees / it sees — to perceive with the eyes, and by extension to have insight or discernment.
11.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb of the causative Form IV (its base means 'to see', so this is the transitive 'to make see / perceive'); the Form IV shape shows in the silent first root letter and the 'i' vowel before the last root letter (yuCCiCu). The 'yu-' marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, used for ongoing or factual statements ('he sees').
11.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, vision, perception, insight

12.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'it avails, suffices, benefits, or makes free from need' — to be of use against something or to enrich and relieve someone of need. The root centres on richness, sufficiency, and being free of want.
13.grammar: An ongoing or future action. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the form (causative pattern) carries the sense of 'to make sufficient' or 'to be of avail'. The final long -ī is the verb's own weak-root termination.
13.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, sufficient

14.meaning: With you / about you / from you — the preposition ʿan ('away from, about, concerning') joined to 'you' (one male); after a verb of being pleased it carries the sense 'pleased WITH you'.
14.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. ʿan basically means moving away from, or 'about/concerning' a topic; paired with a verb of contentment it yields 'pleased with'. The suffix -ka is the second-person masculine singular object ('you', one male). Together: 'with you / concerning you'.

15.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

1.meaning: An affectionate vocative meaning 'O my father' — a tender form of address to one's father, where the original possessive 'my' is replaced by a final -i that carries the same intimate sense.
1.grammar: A vocative: the particle 'yā' is used to call or address someone. The ending -ati (with its final -i) is a special endearing form used when addressing one's father; the -i here stands in for the dropped possessive pronoun 'my', so the whole means 'O my father'.
1.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — fatherhood

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: He / it came to me — a past act of someone or something arriving or coming to the speaker.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'), shown by its bare form with the final 'a' vowel. The attached '-nī' is the object pronoun 'me' (the 'n' here cushions the verb before the 'me' ending), so the whole means 'he/it came to me'.

5.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: The knowledge; sure and certain knowing, established information and understanding (with the definite article).
6.grammar: A definite verbal noun: al- means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship. It denotes knowledge as a settled, certain thing.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

8.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
8.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: It comes to you / let it come to you — a present-tense act of something reaching or arriving to the person addressed.
9.grammar: An imperfect verb with the 'ya-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), from a root with a weak final letter. The stem ends in a short '-i' with no long vowel because it is in the jussive, the mood used after conditional or negative particles (the weak final letter drops in the jussive). The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular).

10.meaning: So follow me! — a command to come after, walk behind, take as a guide, and obey, addressed to one person, with an introductory 'so/then'.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) verb of the Form-VIII pattern ('to follow, take as a guide'), addressed to a single person, shown by the bare stem with no subject ending. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so' or 'then', linking it to what precedes. The attached '-nī' is the object pronoun 'me'.
10.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

11.meaning: I will guide you / let me guide you — to lead someone on the right way, show the correct path, addressed to one person, with the speaker as the guide.
11.grammar: An imperfect verb with the 'a-' prefix marking a first-person singular subject ('I'), from a root with a weak final letter. The stem ends in a short '-i' (jussive mood, in which the weak final letter drops), the form used in answers to commands or conditions ('… I will guide you'). The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular).
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

12.meaning: 'A path', 'a way', 'a road' — a clear route or way that one travels, often used for a course of conduct or a way of life.
12.grammar: A noun. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation ('a path', not 'the path'); the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb.

13.meaning: Even, straight, and well-balanced — sound and upright in form, level and properly proportioned, walking erect on a straight course.
13.grammar: An adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern meaning 'even / straight / sound'. The final '-an' (tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative, a form often used to describe the state or manner of someone or something ('walking upright, on a level path').
13.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, level, straight, well-proportioned

1.meaning: An affectionate vocative meaning 'O my father' — a tender form of address to one's father, where the original possessive 'my' is replaced by a final -i that carries the same intimate sense.
1.grammar: A vocative: the particle 'yā' is used to call or address someone. The ending -ati (with its final -i) is a special endearing form used when addressing one's father; the -i here stands in for the dropped possessive pronoun 'my', so the whole means 'O my father'.
1.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — fatherhood

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: You worship / you serve — to direct devotion and obedient submission toward an object of worship (addressed to one person).
3.grammar: An imperfect verb with the 'ta-' prefix marking a second-person singular subject ('you'). The verb is in the jussive, the mood used after prohibitive or conditional particles (e.g. 'do not worship…'). A sound Form I jussive normally ends in a vowelless final letter (sukūn); the short '-i' appears here as the jussive vowel that breaks up the consonant cluster formed with the following word.
3.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit in devotion

4.meaning: The Shayṭān / the Satan — the rebellious, evil one who tempts and misleads; broadly any defiant, alienating force that incites toward wrong.
4.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative case, which most often signals the word is the direct object of a verb. (The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'sh' in pronunciation.)
4.root: Disputed in classical lexicography. Many derive it from ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — being far/remote and rebellious (hence one distant from good and given to defiance), treating the final nūn as radical. Others derive it from ش-ي-ط (sh-y-ṭ), from شَاطَ 'to burn, blaze, perish', treating the nūn as an added letter. Both are attested (e.g., in Lisān al-ʿArab).

5.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
5.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

6.meaning: The Shayṭān / the Satan — the rebellious, evil one who tempts and misleads; broadly any defiant, alienating force that incites toward wrong.
6.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative case, which most often signals the word is the direct object of a verb. (The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'sh' in pronunciation.)
6.root: Disputed in classical lexicography. Many derive it from ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — being far/remote and rebellious (hence one distant from good and given to defiance), treating the final nūn as radical. Others derive it from ش-ي-ط (sh-y-ṭ), from شَاطَ 'to burn, blaze, perish', treating the nūn as an added letter. Both are attested (e.g., in Lisān al-ʿArab).

7.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

7.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

8.meaning: 'To / for the All-Merciful.' Al-Rahman is a divine name of Allah denoting the One whose mercy is vast, all-embracing, and overflowing to the whole of creation; the prefixed 'to/for' directs an action or dedication toward Him.
8.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('to / for'). Because li- demands the genitive case, the noun takes the final -i ending. The article al- assimilates into the following 'r' sound (heard as ar-Rahman). The form al-Rahman is an intensive pattern signifying overwhelming, all-encompassing mercy.
8.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tenderness

9.meaning: Disobedient, rebellious; one who refuses to comply and persistently defies. The intensive form points to defiance as a settled disposition rather than a single act.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a strong or characteristic quality ('thoroughly disobedient'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking it as an indefinite word in object/predicate position.

1.meaning: An affectionate vocative meaning 'O my father' — a tender form of address to one's father, where the original possessive 'my' is replaced by a final -i that carries the same intimate sense.
1.grammar: A vocative: the particle 'yā' is used to call or address someone. The ending -ati (with its final -i) is a special endearing form used when addressing one's father; the -i here stands in for the dropped possessive pronoun 'my', so the whole means 'O my father'.
1.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — fatherhood

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: It touches you / lest it touch you — for something (often harm or affliction) to reach, afflict, or come into contact with the person addressed.
5.grammar: An imperfect verb with the 'ya-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The doubled middle/final consonant (shadda on the 's') reflects the doubled root (m-s-s). The final '-a' is a subjunctive ending, the form used after particles meaning 'lest' or 'so that'. The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular).
5.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, come into contact with, afflict

6.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: The Most Merciful, the All-Compassionate — a name of Allah on an intensive pattern stressing immense, all-embracing mercy that encompasses the whole of creation. It denotes overflowing, universal compassion rather than an occasional act of kindness.
8.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'; its 'l' assimilates in pronunciation into the following 'r' (heard as ar-raḥmān). The word is an intensive form on the faʿlān pattern, conveying fullness and vastness of the quality. The final -i is the genitive ending, used when a word follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… OF …').
8.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion

9.meaning: So that you become / then you will be — the verb 'to be/become', set up as a consequence ('and so you end up being...').
9.grammar: A present verb of 'being' introduced by fa- ('so/then') marking a resulting consequence. The verb is in the subjunctive mood (shown by the -a vowel: -kūna), which here expresses the intended or resulting outcome that follows from what precedes. The ta- prefix marks the doer as 'you' (one male).
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, become, come into being

10.meaning: To / for the Shayṭān — directed toward Satan, the rebellious deceiver who incites people away from Allah. The 'to/for' marks him as the one toward whom something is directed.
10.grammar: A noun with the attached preposition 'li-' ('to' or 'for') and the definite article 'al-'. The final '-i' ending is genitive, the case automatically taken by a noun after a preposition. (Note: the shadda seen on the shīn comes from the word's own root doubling/spelling, not from the article — shīn is a 'moon letter', so the 'l' of al- is fully pronounced: al-shayṭān, not ash-shayṭān.)
10.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote/rebellious; the root behind 'Shayṭān', the adversary

11.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.
11.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, alliance, friendship

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: Are you one who turns away in dislike? — an opening question ('are…?') joined to 'one who is averse / desirous'; the word names a person who feels aversion toward, or shrinks back from, something.

parts.en: one who turns away in dislike (or one who desires)

2.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun, pattern fāʿil) naming the person who does the action, prefixed with the question particle 'a-' ('are…?'). The '-un' ending (tanwīn, the '-n' sound) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case — the case used for the subject or for a stand-alone predicate.
2.root: ر-غ-ب (r-gh-b) — desire, inclination; with 'away from', aversion

3.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
3.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

4.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

5.meaning: My gods / my deities — objects taken and worshipped as gods, marked as belonging to the speaker.
5.grammar: A plural noun ('gods') with the attached possessive '-ī' meaning 'my'. When this 'my' ending is added, it replaces the word's normal case vowel, so case is understood from context rather than shown by the ending.
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship; the root of 'ilāh' (a god) and 'Allāh'

6.meaning: O Ibrahim (Abraham): the prophet's name addressed directly with the call-word 'O'.
6.grammar: A vocative (direct-address) phrase: yā is the call-particle 'O'. The final -u marks the noun being called by name. As a proper name it has no root.

7.meaning: An emphatic conditional opener combining an oath-like emphasis with 'if' — roughly 'most certainly, if (such-and-such happens)…', strongly stressing the condition and the response that follows.
7.grammar: Two particles fused together: an emphatic la- that signals a coming oath or strong assertion, plus in ('if') introducing a condition. Together they set up an emphatic 'if… then surely…' construction. Neither has a case ending; particles do not inflect.
7.root: — (particles)

8.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
8.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

9.meaning: You cease / you desist / you stop yourself — to refrain from and put an end to an action one was doing (addressed to one person).

parts.en: desist / refrain / come to an end

9.grammar: An imperfect verb of the Form-VIII pattern ('to desist, refrain'), with the 'ta-' prefix marking a second-person singular subject ('you'), from a root with a weak final letter. The short final '-i' (with the weak final letter dropped) marks the jussive mood, used after conditional particles such as 'if you do not…'.
9.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, restrain; to come to an end, desist

10.meaning: I will most certainly stone you — an emphatic, double-stressed promise by the speaker to pelt the person addressed with stones (to drive away or punish).
10.grammar: An imperfect verb wrapped in two layers of emphasis: the prefixed 'la-' ('surely') and the heavy '-nna' ending (the 'emphatic nūn'), which together turn the verb into a strong, oath-like assertion about the future. The 'a-' prefix marks a first-person subject ('I'); the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular).
10.root: ر-ج-م (r-j-m) — to stone, pelt with stones; to drive away

11.meaning: And keep away from me / and forsake me — a command to depart from, abandon, or shun the speaker, with an introductory 'and'.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person, shown by the bare stem with no subject ending, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The attached '-nī' is the object pronoun 'me' (the 'n' cushions the verb before the 'me' ending).
11.root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r) — to depart, forsake, abandon, shun

12.meaning: For a long stretch of time — for an extended period; can also carry the sense of 'safely / unharmed' for that duration.
12.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The '-an' ending (tanwīn, the '-n' sound) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case; the accusative is the case Arabic uses to turn a word into an adverb of time or manner ('for a long while').
12.root: م-ل-و (m-l-w) — length/extent of time; a long duration

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

2.meaning: Peace, soundness, safety, well-being — freedom from harm and discord; a word of greeting and of the wholeness and security that comes from being safe and at peace.
2.grammar: A noun. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative: the -u marks the nominative (the form a subject or a stated/announced word takes), and the final -n ('tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('peace', not 'the peace').

3.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

4.meaning: I shall ask forgiveness — the speaker's future act of seeking pardon and protection from the consequences of sin, with 'shall/will' built in.
4.grammar: An imperfect verb of the Form-X pattern, whose meaning is 'to seek/ask for' the root idea — here, to seek forgiveness. The prefixed 'sa-' marks the near future ('shall/will'). The 'a-' prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'), and the final '-u' is the indicative ending for a plain future statement.
4.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, pardon, cover over (sins)

5.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
5.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
5.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

6.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
6.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

7.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
7.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

8.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

9.meaning: 'In me / with me.' A preposition fused with the first-person singular pronoun, expressing attachment, belief, or trust directed toward the speaker ('me').
9.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). The -ī here is the first-person singular object that always follows a preposition or noun; it does not change for case. Combined sense: 'in me' or 'with me.'

10.meaning: Ever-gracious and kindly attentive — describing one who is gentle, well-disposed, and deeply caring, responding to requests with warm favor.
10.grammar: An adjective in the intensive pattern (faʿīl), conveying a deep, constant quality. The '-an' ending (tanwīn, the '-n' sound) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for objects and for predicates after certain verbs ('… is ever-gracious').
10.root: ح-ف-و / ح-ف-ي (ḥ-f-w/y) — to be kind, attentive, solicitous; to honor with care

1.meaning: And I withdraw from you all / and I will keep apart from you — the speaker's act of separating himself and standing aside from a group, with an introductory 'and'.
1.grammar: An imperfect verb of the Form-VIII pattern ('to withdraw, set oneself apart'), prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The 'a-' prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'), and the '-u' before the pronoun is the indicative vowel for a plain present/future statement. The attached '-kum' is the object 'you all' (masculine plural).
1.root: ع-ز-ل (ʿ-z-l) — to set apart, isolate, withdraw, remove

2.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
2.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
3.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
5.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
5.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: And I call upon / and I will invoke — the speaker's act of calling on, supplicating, and appealing to someone (typically in prayer), with an introductory 'and'.
7.grammar: An imperfect verb with the 'a-' prefix marking a first-person singular subject ('I'), prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'), from a root with a weak final letter. The stem ends in a long '-ū' (the weak final root letter realized as a long vowel), and the spelling carries a silent 'alif' after it — a conventional spelling after this verb form. It reads as a plain statement, 'and I call upon'.
7.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

8.meaning: My Lord — 'Rabb' is the Master and Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures, and governs all things; with '-ī' it is claimed by the speaker as 'my Lord'.
8.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with the attached possessive '-ī' meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending takes the place of the word's normal case vowel, so case is understood from context rather than marked on the ending.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, mastery, nurturing care, sustaining

9.meaning: It may be that / perhaps — a verb of approximation expressing hopeful expectation or near-likelihood that something will come about. When used of Allah it conveys an outcome that is sure to be realized rather than mere doubt.
9.grammar: A verb of approximation (one of the 'verbs of hoping/nearness'), defective and non-conjugating: it stays fixed in this form and does not change for tense or person. Its final -ā reflects the underlying weak root letter. It introduces an expected or hoped-for possibility, typically followed by a clause stating what may occur.
9.root: ع-س-و / ع-س-ي (ʿ-s-w/y) — to be hoped for, to be near (verb of approximation/hope)

10.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
10.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

11.meaning: '(that) I be / I should be' — the verb 'to be/become' in the first person, used in a dependent sense ('that I be…', 'lest I be…'). It expresses entering into or belonging to a described state.

parts.en: be / become (stem, ending in the subjunctive vowel -a)

11.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be/become' with the 'I' prefix (a-). The stem ends in the third root letter ن, which carries the final short vowel -a; this -a is the subjunctive ending, the form used after particles such as 'that', 'so that', or 'lest' — so it reads 'that I be / I should be' rather than the plain statement 'I am' (which would end in -u).
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

12.meaning: With / by the calling upon — by means of the act of invoking, supplicating, or appealing to someone (the 'bi-' marks it as the means or instrument).
12.grammar: A noun ('supplication') with the attached preposition 'bi-' ('with' or 'by'). The final '-i' ending is genitive, the case a noun automatically takes after a preposition; it commonly also links a noun to a following noun ('… of …').
12.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, supplicate, appeal

13.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
13.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

14.meaning: Wretched, miserable, ill-fated, deprived of good; one who fails or is left disappointed. The opposite of blessed and successful.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the accusative with nunation, indefinite. In this case it commonly serves as a predicate-complement of certain verbs ('was/became wretched') or describes an accusative noun; the nunation marks it indefinite.
14.root: ش-ق-و / ش-ق-ي (sh-q-w / sh-q-y) — to be wretched, suffer hardship

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he withdrew from them' or 'he kept himself apart from them' — to deliberately distance oneself, go aside, and separate from a group of people.
2.grammar: A Form VIII (iftaʿala) past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The Form VIII pattern adds a reflexive sense of doing the action to or for oneself ('he removed himself'). The attached -hum is an object pronoun meaning 'them', so the whole word reads 'he withdrew from them'.
2.root: ع-ز-ل (ʿ-z-l) — to set aside, separate, isolate

3.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
3.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

4.meaning: Means 'they worship / they serve in devotion' — a present-tense verb for the ongoing act of worship: humble service, obedience, and devotion directed to a deity.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they (masculine plural) do …'. The full -ūna ending also marks the verb as a plain statement of fact (indicative), as opposed to a shortened form used after certain particles.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we granted / we bestowed (as a gift)' — to give freely and graciously, without expecting return.
8.grammar: A Form I past-tense verb with the suffix -nā, which marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The opening wa- is the connective 'and'. So the form means 'and we bestowed'.
8.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to grant as a gift

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: Isaac (Isḥāq) — the proper name of the prophet, son of Abraham.
10.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is a 'diptote', meaning it takes the '-a' ending for both the accusative (direct object) and genitive cases and never takes nunation ('-an').
10.root: — (proper name, no Arabic root)

11.meaning: The proper name 'Jacob' (Yaʿqūb), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
11.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; as a foreign (non-Arabic) name it is 'diptote,' taking -a for both those cases and never taking nunation (the -n sound).
11.root: — (proper name)

12.meaning: 'And all / each one' — referring comprehensively to every member of a group, 'each and every.'
12.grammar: 'And' + the totality-word kull ('all/each'). The '-an' (nunation) is the accusative indefinite ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). Standing alone with nunation, kull means 'each one / all of them.'

13.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
13.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

14.meaning: 'A prophet' — one whom Allah inspires and sends with revelation to guide people; a bearer of divine news and message.
14.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (with tanwin) is accusative and indefinite ('a prophet'); the accusative commonly marks the object of making/appointing or a predicate after certain verbs ('He made [me] a prophet').
14.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; one who brings news (a prophet)

1.meaning: 'And We bestowed / granted' — to give freely as a gift or favour, with no expectation of return, prefixed with 'and'.

parts.en: bestowed, granted as a gift (past stem)

1.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', giving 'and we bestowed'.
1.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: 'Our mercy' — mercy meaning tender compassion, kindness, and the active giving of relief and favour, possessed by 'us'.
4.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the attached possessive pronoun -nā ('our'), which puts the noun in the construct (possessed) state. The -i vowel (kasra) before the pronoun is the construct-state linking vowel that joins the noun to its attached possessor; together they yield 'our mercy'.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
5.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: Literally 'tongue', and by extension 'language', 'speech', or a 'spoken reputation' — the mention or renown a person leaves in the speech of others.
7.grammar: A masculine noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise governed by it.
7.root: ل-س-ن (l-s-n) — tongue, language, speech

8.meaning: Truthfulness, sincerity, genuineness — the quality of what is true and reliable. As the second word of a possessive phrase it lends the sense 'a true/sound/honourable ...'.
8.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-in' ending (doubled kasra, tanwīn) marks the genitive case for an indefinite noun — it typically shows that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('... OF truth') or follows a preposition.
8.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity

9.meaning: 'High', 'lofty', 'exalted' — an adjective describing something elevated in rank, status, or sublimity.
